title: Technical Program Manager, Revenue Operations
description:
ABOUT PLEO

At Pleo, we believe that finance is the strategic force at the heart of how every business runs. When a finance team leads with its craft, they make better decisions and steer the business with more confidence. In order to do that, the busywork that comes with expense management needs to move out the way.

That’s why we built a spend management platform that streamlines the whole process, from employee spending to approvals and reconciliation. Finance teams get clarity and control of all the numbers and data in one place and employees get an experience that they actually enjoy.

The word “Pleo” in Greek means “more than you’d expect,” and that mindset has driven our growth since 2015 and our 40,000+ customers. Today we’re 750+ people from over 65 nationalities who take pride in understanding customer needs, turning complex problems into simple solutions, challenging the way things are done, and aiming for the highest outcome. We haven’t got everything figured out, but we’re committed to developing and delivering an experience as elevated as the craft of finance.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager, Revenue Operations to join our Revenue Operations at Pleo. In this role, you'll help build the technical and operational infrastructure that enables Pleo’s revenue organisation to scale and be part of cross-functional programs as we scale Pleo's customer and revenue lifecycle. If you're excited about solving complex architectural challenges at the intersection of business systems and data and are passionate about SaaS, fintech, and modern Revenue Operations, then this is the opportunity for you!




WHO YOU’LL BE WORKING WITH AND REPORTING TO 

You’ll report to our Director of Revenue Operations and work closely with teams in Sales, Customer Success, Customer Experience, Marketing, and Customer Onboarding. Our team of Revenue Operations professionals is highly collaborative and dedicated to building a scalable, reliable, and connected revenue operating system. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across Product, Engineering, Data and Analytics, Business Systems, and Finance to ensure success.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

As a Technical Program Manager, Revenue Operations, you will:

 - Lead complex technical programs across the revenue technology ecosystem – from discovery and requirements definition through architecture design, implementation, UAT, launch, and post-launch adoption.

 - Translate requirements bidirectionally – turn complex commercial challenges into precise technical specs for Engineering and Data teams, while breaking down technical trade-offs, system dependencies, and risks for business stakeholders.

 - Drive revenue systems and CRM initiatives – optimize architecture and end-to-end data flows across lead-to-opportunity, sales-to-onboarding handoffs, renewal, churn risk, and billing operations.

 - Identify and eliminate technical and operational debt – architect future-state solutions rather than quick fixes, automating manual workflows and improving data integrity across critical revenue systems.

 - Champion modern automation and AI-enabled RevOps capabilities – integrate intelligent workflows, predictive customer health signals, and agent-based workflows to accelerate commercial productivity.

 


WHAT YOU BRING 


You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

 - 5+ years of Technical Program Management experience – a proven track record of managing complex technical programs involving multi-system integrations, data models, APIs, and technical dependencies.

 - A strong understanding of the SDLC and revenue mechanics – deep comfort with software development workflows (Agile/hybrid) paired with a solid grasp of the B2B revenue lifecycle (lead routing, pipeline, onboarding, retention, expansion).

 - System architecture fluency – the ability to challenge technical designs, evaluate failure scenarios, define sources of truth, and ensure long-term scalability.

 - Exceptional stakeholder management and influence – strong executive communication skills, high cross-functional influence without direct authority, and the ability to lead governance, risk tracking, and UAT.

 - Experience with HubSpot or another enterprise CRM, modern data warehouses (SQL querying), CPQ/billing tools, or integration middleware.

 - A background in SaaS, fintech, payments, spend management, or a high-growth digital environment.

 


WHY IS THIS ROLE A GOOD FIT FOR YOU

This role is a good fit for you if:

 - You love being the technical bridge between revenue leaders and software/data engineers, translating strategy into scalable technical execution.

 - You think in systems, data flows, and dependencies, and prefer fixing root causes rather than patching symptoms.

 - You want true ownership of strategic programs and enjoy driving them through technical delivery to measurable business adoption.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

 - Your TPM experience is primarily administrative (focused only on timelines, meeting notes, and status reports without understanding the underlying technical architecture).

 - You are uncomfortable discussing APIs, data schemas, integrations, and failure modes directly with engineers.

 - You need fully defined requirements handed to you rather than proactively untangling ambiguity and challenging assumptions.
   
   


HOW YOU’LL DEVELOP IN THIS ROLE 

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

 - Map Pleo's revenue systems landscape, data flows, and sources of truth, taking ownership of active high-priority technical initiatives.

 - Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Data, and commercial leaders to streamline requirements gathering, UAT, and release governance.

 - Grow your skills in scaling cutting-edge RevOps infrastructure, introducing automation and AI-enabled workflows as Pleo expands across markets.




THE LOCATION


Please note: We can hire on a hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.




SHOW ME THE BENEFITS!



 - Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

 - Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

 - Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

 - 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).

 - For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

 - We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

 - Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work



THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

 1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

 2. Hiring Manager Interview: A 45-minute interview with the hiring manager to go deeper on your experience and how your profile fits the role.

 3. Pleo Challenge: A take-home test followed by a 60-minute team interview. This is your opportunity to show us how you'd handle the day-to-day of the role (e.g., designing a programme, measuring impact, stakeholder communication).

 4. Final Interview: A final interview with a Senior Leader

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for this role, we received a vast number applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

 - CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

 - Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

 - Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.


ABOUT YOUR APPLICATION

 - English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

 - A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

 - Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

 - Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.

 - Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here https://www.pleo.io/en/legal.

 - Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

 - Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

title: Sales Operations Business Partner
description:

In order to do that, the busywork that comes with expense management needs to move out the way.

The word “Pleo” in Greek means “more than you’d expect,” and that mindset has driven our growth since 2015 and our 40,000+ customers. About the role

We’re looking for a Sales Operations Business Partner to sit between our sales leadership and the systems, data, and processes that run the revenue engine. You’ll help the sales team understand where deals stand, where revenue is coming from, and where it’s at risk. You’ll own how we track pipeline, report on performance, and build the dashboards leaders rely on to make decisions. This is a role for someone who thinks in business outcomes first and uses data and tools as the means to get there.

What you’ll do

 - Own pipeline management processes, including stage definitions, forecasting cadence, and hygiene standards, and work with sales managers to keep the pipeline accurate.

 - Build and maintain regular sales reporting covering bookings, pipeline coverage, conversion rates, win/loss, and rep and team performance.

 - Design, build, and maintain dashboards that give leadership and frontline managers a clear view of performance against targets.

 - Act as a business partner to sales leaders: understand their priorities, translate them into operational requirements, and bring data-backed recommendations to planning and business reviews.

 - Support forecasting and quarterly business reviews by preparing the data, challenging assumptions, and flagging risks early.

 - Own day-to-day administration and configuration of the CRM (e.g. Salesforce or HubSpot), including fields, workflows, user access, and reporting structure, in partnership with the RevOps or systems team.

 - Drive adoption of CRM and sales processes by working with managers and reps, and by making the right behaviour the easy one.

 - Support territory, quota, and compensation-related analysis as needed, in partnership with Finance.

 - Identify process gaps and inefficiencies across the sales funnel and lead improvements, documenting changes and training the team on them.

 - Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Finance, Customer Success, and Product Ops to keep data consistent across systems.

What you’ll bring

 - 7+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, GTM operations, or a related commercial role, ideally in a [B2B SaaS / relevant industry] environment.

 - Strong experience with CRM systems, ideally Salesforce or HubSpot, including reporting and basic administration.

 - Solid understanding of sales metrics and funnel dynamics, including pipeline coverage, conversion, forecasting accuracy, and sales cycle length.

 - Proven ability to build clear reports and dashboards in tools such as Excel/Google Sheets, Looker, Tableau, or Power BI. You don’t need to write code, but you should be comfortable working with data and spotting what matters.

 - Experience running pipeline reviews or forecast calls, or supporting leaders who do.

 - A consultative approach: you can listen to a sales leader, ask the right questions, and turn their needs into a practical solution.

 - Strong communication skills, with the ability to present findings clearly to senior stakeholders and explain trade-offs simply.

 - Good judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to balance speed and accuracy.

 - Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities.

Nice to have

 - Experience supporting a sales team through a scaling or transformation phase.

 - Familiarity with sales compensation or territory planning tools.

 - Exposure to revenue analytics or forecasting methodologies.

 - Experience with a BI tool or basic SQL, though this is not required.

 - Experience working with AI tools to create efficiencies within the role.

What success looks like

 - Leadership trusts the pipeline and forecast numbers and uses them to make decisions.

 - Sales managers run their reviews from the dashboards you’ve built, without needing manual reports.

 - CRM data quality improves measurably over time.

 - Sales leaders see you as a partner who brings ideas, not just reports.

title: GTM Engineer, Marketing
description:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We’re trusted by 20,000 leading organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.

In both our product and our workplace, we’re intentional about making work more efficient, flexible, and fulfilling. Tremendous is a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life.

Our customers, who include researchers, marketers, HR teams, and nonprofits, rave about how fast and easy it is to use Tremendous. Check out our ratings on G2 https://www.g2.com/products/tremendous/reviews.

Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. Join us before our next international offsite.



About the role

We're looking for a GTM Engineer focused on marketing who can integrate LLMs, workflow tools, and low-code capabilities to build agentic solutions that automate the highest-leverage workflow problems our marketing team faces. This role will work alongside our brand, content, product marketing, paid, and events marketing teams.



What you'll do

 - Design and build agentic workflows across the full campaign lifecycle, from Product Marketing to Design and Content to Demand Generation.

 - Evaluate and deploy AI tools for marketing. Run structured pilots, then operationalize what works from campaign ideation to execution and analysis.

 - Work with the Data team to build automated reporting pipelines that aggregate cross-channel marketing performance across paid, organic, email, and event channels into a unified view.

 - Build AI-assisted lead scoring and qualification with the marketing planner.

 - Let marketers run channel work from AI agents: paid campaign optimizations, creative uploads, and lifecycle campaign setup in HubSpot.

 - Build reusable tools and workflows that marketers can run themselves. Make the whole team faster rather than becoming a bottleneck.



What you'll bring

 - 5-8 years in marketing operations, marketing technology, or GTM engineering. You understand campaign lifecycles and channel reporting because you've lived them.

 - You build the zero-to-one. Workflows stitched across tools where the inputs are messy and the judgment calls are real, rather than maintained applications on a custom code base.

 - Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs, AI agent frameworks, and workflow automation tools (Cargo, Zapier, Make, n8n, or similar). You've shipped agentic workflows, not just experimented with them.

 - Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, and basic scripting. You don't stop when the no-code tool runs out of options.

 - Process-first thinker. Your instinct is to map the workflow and find where it breaks before naming the tool that fixes it.

 - Bias for rapid experimentation. Launch, measure, iterate weekly.

 - Strong written communication. We're a documentation-first culture.

 - Autonomous and self-directed. Tremendous is not a great fit for people who default to waiting for instructions.

 - High empathy. You care about your teammates and users.



Nice to haves

 - Marketing-specific AI tools (Writer, AirOps, Phrase, etc.)

 - SaaS martech stacks (HubSpot, Salesforce, CDPs, ABM platforms)

 - SQL and Snowflake for reporting pipelines

 - Brand or creative operations background. You understand how designers work and what makes a good brief.

 - Cursor, Claude, or similar AI-assisted development tools



What's cool about the role

 - Immediate, measurable impact. The problems are concrete and the wins are visible in weeks.

 - The team is already AI-forward. Cursor daily, monthly AI tool evaluations, leadership fully bought in.

 - Profitable and growing without outside investors.

 - Competitive pay, equity, and benefits. Base salary: $135,000 to $180,000.

 - We're a fully remote company. This role is US Remote.

 - We've got smart people and a great culture. See our company handbook https://handbook.tremendous.com/.

About the role

We're looking for a GTM Engineering Manager to lead our team of GTM engineers. Our Revenue Operations team works like a product and engineering org: planners define what marketing, sales, and customer success need, and GTM engineers design and build it with LLMs, workflow tools, and code. You'll own how that team works: its standards, its infrastructure, and the growth of the people on it. You'll stay hands-on, building the systems that make the whole team faster.



What you'll do

 - Manage and develop a team of GTM engineers across marketing, sales, and platform work. Hire the next ones.

 - Set the team's engineering practices: version control, review, documentation, and ownership for every workflow, agent, and integration in production.

 - Build the team's own infrastructure, including the agents and tooling that keep work assigned, tracked, and current.

 - Partner with GTM planners on the roadmap: bring the build-side view on what's feasible and how to sequence it, and put the right builder on the right project.

 - Act as the team's ambassador to our AI enablement engineering team, and shape how work moves from a GTM engineering prototype to long-term engineering ownership.

 - Own relationships with the technical vendors the team builds on, such as Cargo.



What you'll bring

 - 7+ years across RevOps, GTM engineering, marketing or sales ops engineering, or internal tools, with real hands-on building.

 - 2+ years managing builders or technical roles, with people you've grown into stronger roles.

 - You're a capable builder yourself: AI agents, workflow tools (Cargo, Clay, n8n, Zapier, or similar), APIs, webhooks, and Git.

 - Engineering-manager instincts: you've set up review, documentation, and rollback practices on systems other people depend on.

 - Fluency across the GTM funnel: marketing, sales, and customer success.

 - Strong written communication. We're a documentation-first culture.

 - Autonomous and self-directed. Tremendous is not a great fit for people who default to waiting for instructions.

 - High empathy. You care about your teammates and the people who use what your team builds.



Nice to haves

 - HubSpot depth, especially workflows and APIs

 - Cursor, Claude, or similar AI-assisted development as a daily habit

 - SQL and Snowflake

 - Experience standing up a GTM engineering or RevOps engineering team from a few people

 - Usage-based or fintech GTM experience



What's cool about the role

 - The team already exists and is shipping. You're making a strong team faster, not starting from scratch.

 - The company is AI-forward. Cursor daily, regular AI tool evaluations, leadership fully bought in.

 - Profitable and growing without outside investors.

 - Competitive pay, equity, and benefits. Base salary: $190,000-$230,000

 - Fully remote. This role is US Remote.

 - Smart people and a great culture. See our company handbook https://handbook.tremendous.com/.

title: GTM Engineer (Pacific Time)
description:
Location: Fully Remote (Pacific time zones)
Start Date: ASAP
Languages: Fluent English required
Industry: AI / Data Infrastructure
Team: Go-to-Market (GTM)
Type: Full-time




ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

Pragmatike is hiring a GTM Engineer on behalf of a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data.

Its marketplace connects data providers with leading AI companies, including startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier AI labs. Backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator, the company is scaling rapidly and expanding its commercial operations.

The company operates a two-sided marketplace where leading AI labs specify the data they need, and the commercial team identifies businesses and individuals who can provide it. As the business grows, the focus is shifting towards building the systems and infrastructure needed to scale these operations efficiently.

As a GTM Engineer, you'll approach go-to-market as an engineering challenge. You'll own the technical infrastructure behind the commercial team, building data pipelines, automations, integrations and internal tools that help a lean team source, qualify and close opportunities at scale.

This is an engineering-first role with a strong commercial focus, ideal for someone who enjoys building practical systems, solving operational bottlenecks and working closely with sales teams and founders.

The company has offices in San Francisco and Singapore, with remote opportunities also available. Working hours will align with either Singapore or US Pacific business hours, depending on your location.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the GTM tooling stack end to end, including selecting, configuring, integrating and maintaining the tools used by the commercial team.

 - Build scalable sourcing systems, including scrapers and data enrichment pipelines, to identify relevant data providers and opportunities.

 - Develop and maintain the data infrastructure behind GTM, connecting CRM, marketplace and product data into a reliable source of truth for pipeline, listings and revenue.

 - Build internal tools to support provider research, listing quality checks, pipeline management and sales forecasting.

 - Automate repetitive workflows across sourcing, qualification, lead routing and reporting.

 - Identify operational bottlenecks with the founders and commercial team, prioritising automation projects with the highest impact.

 - Explore and implement AI agents where they provide clear advantages over traditional automation.

 - Make build-versus-buy decisions for GTM tooling, keeping the technical stack efficient, reliable and easy to maintain.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2+ years of professional software engineering experience.

 - Strong programming skills in Python or TypeScript, with fluent SQL.

 - Experience building internal tools, automations or integrations used by other teams in their day-to-day operations.

 - Hands-on experience developing data pipelines and API integrations between different business systems.

 - Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to translate business needs into practical technical solutions.

 - Commercial awareness and an interest in revenue operations, with the ability to understand sales workflows and prioritise projects that directly support business growth.

 - Clear written communication skills and the ability to take ownership in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.



Nice to Have:

 - Experience in RevOps, growth engineering, sales engineering or forward-deployed engineering.

 - Hands-on experience implementing LLMs or AI agents in production environments.

 - Previous experience in an early-stage startup or as a founder.

 - Familiarity with AI training data, including RL environments, evaluations and benchmarks.

We're open to motivated candidates who don't meet every requirement. Strong engineering fundamentals, ownership and the ability to learn quickly are what matter most.




WHY THIS OPPORTUNITY

 - Build systems that drive revenue: Develop the tools, integrations and pipelines that power the entire commercial operation.

 - High impact in a lean team: Automate critical workflows and help a small GTM team operate at significantly greater scale.

 - Work directly with founders: Collaborate closely with the founding and commercial teams, identifying problems and deciding what is worth building.

 - Work with modern AI tooling: Explore and implement AI agents and automation solutions where they deliver real operational value.

 - Flexible working setup: Choose between on-site opportunities in San Francisco or Singapore, or remote work aligned with Singapore or US Pacific business hours.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & PRIVACY

Pragmatike is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants without discrimination. We recruit on behalf of our clients and prohibit discrimination and harassment based on race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

We are committed to a fair and inclusive hiring process. We process your personal data solely for recruitment purposes, in accordance with applicable privacy laws, and maintain reasonable safeguards to protect your information. Your data may be shared with our client(s) for hiring consideration, but will not be disclosed to third parties outside of the recruitment process.

title: Senior Director, Revenue Operations
description:
About Us:

Wrapbook is the AI platform for production finance. We’re building a system of action that puts finance teams in control of their whole production, from payroll, to spend, to accounting. 

Built for feature films, TV, and commercials, Wrapbook is trusted by teams at Netflix, Paramount, Anonymous Content, and more. With backing from Andreessen Horowitz, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, our team of 350+ is using AI to transform how finance teams work and empower them to do more with less.




The Opportunity – Senior Director, Revenue Operations (Remote - USA / Canada)

Wrapbook is building the financial infrastructure of the project economy, and we're looking for a Revenue Operations leader to run the engine behind our go-to-market and post-sale motion. If you want to build a modern, AI-forward revenue operations function and the team to run it, this is the job for you.

Reporting to the CFO, you will own the bookings forecast, sales compensation and operations, marketing operations, and the technology platform that underpins our GTM and post sales efforts. You will own our Salesforce platform, setting its architecture and standards while working with and through the Salesforce admins on the RevOps team and on teams across the company.

You’ll lead an AI-native GTM function, building on one source of truth, a visible roadmap, and clear standards. You’ll lead through a team and stay technical enough to set a credible roadmap and make architectural decisions.

You'll sit in Finance and serve Sales, Marketing and Client Ops. Your primary colleagues are the leaders of those orgs, and your job is to make them faster and their numbers trustworthy. You will lead a team of ~6-8 that keeps the system and operations accurate, fast, and improving.

What You'll Do

Run the revenue engine

 - Own the bookings forecast: definitions (pipeline, bookings, commit / best case / upside), cadence, pipeline health, and deal inspection.

 - Run the operating rhythm of the revenue team: pipeline reviews, forecast calls, and the revenue inputs to MBRs, QBRs, and board materials

 - Own GTM planning: territories, segmentation, and quota and capacity modeling

 - Oversee sales compensation operations: provide input on plan design, and manage the process to ensure accurate, on-time payouts with the controls a financial process requires

 - Oversee the deal desk process: approvals, structures, and non-standard terms, in partnership with Strategic Finance on complex-deal pricing

 - Own marketing ops: tech stack, pipeline and performance metrics

 - Be proactive and opinionated with Sales leadership: surface risks to the numbers, and bring recommendations to keep things on track

Lead the AI-forward GTM roadmap

 - Manage the AI sales and marketing roadmap from start to finish: partner with Sales and Marketing leadership to turn their vision into a sequenced, shippable roadmap of AI workflows and agents

 - Decide on design of the tech stack: build vs buy, app vs Salesforce enabled workflows, etc.

 - Own milestones and adoption of what ships: measured use and business impact count

 - Report AI adoption and success metrics: use a data driven approach to track adoption and agent-attributable outcomes (pipeline lift, cycle time, forecast accuracy)

Own Salesforce as the system of record

 - Own Salesforce architecture: the core object model, the sandbox and release path, and sign-off on deeper work (schema, Apex, complex Flow, integrations)

 - Own all development on core objects and large builds. Define the line between light and large builds, and sign off that large builds fit our architecture

 - Partner with the Salesforce admins in Sales, Marketing and Client Ops, who own light builds, through a single intake and agreed SLAs

 - Own data integrity at the source: field definitions written in plain language, validation and hygiene standards, protected closed periods, and a logged process for corrections

 - Own the Salesforce side of every data handoff: partner with Analytics and Finance so Salesforce data flows as expected to the warehouse and BI tools

Lead the team and maintain cross functional alignment

 - Lead and develop a team of ~7 across sales operations, marketing ops, and builders (SFDC and AI): a leader of leaders, with hiring, coaching, and accountability that scales

 - Stay builder-literate (about 20% of your time): prototype the hard net-new problem and review work to stay credible. Success is measured by what the team delivers, what people adopt, and improved efficiency in our GTM processes

 - Set clear priorities for the team and share them broadly: run one front door for requests, say what new work costs and what it displaces, and keep a roadmap that Sales, Marketing, Client Ops and Finance can see. Business owners decide what matters most; you make the tradeoffs visible and ensure cross functional partners understand timing and status.

 - Set and enforce standards for admins and builders embedded in Sales, Marketing and Client Ops: change path, field definitions, and release review, so one source of truth holds as teams build.

 

What You'll Have

 - 10+ years in Revenue, Sales, or GTM Operations at a high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech company, including 4+ years leading teams and leaders

 - Deep Salesforce command: architecture, data model, release management, and the judgment to know what to build, buy, or configure

 - Strong financial fluency: forecasting, bookings and unit economics, compensation modeling, and board-level revenue reporting

 - Builder-literate: comfortable with SQL and a modern data warehouse, workflow and orchestration tools, and LLM and agent tooling, enough to set a real technical roadmap and earn builders' respect

 - Experience governing a shared system (ideally Salesforce) that admins and builders in other business units also work in: you’ve set and enforced standards for schema, release path, and data definitions, and made them stick without direct authority over those admins.

 - Hands-on experience using AI to change how a GTM function works, with specific tools and specific outcomes, not just familiarity

 - A track record of change management and influence: you can effectively prioritize cross functionally and can push back on a revenue leader when hygiene slips

 - Excellent, exec-ready verbal and written communication skills: you start with the decision and the impact, and provide updates that give visibility to complex projects

 - Growth mindset and builder mentality: you're energized by ambiguity and keep raising the bar as the company scales

Nice to have

 - Python and agentic coding tools; modern data stack (Snowflake, dbt, a BI/semantic layer); conversation-intelligence platforms; commission tooling

 - Experience in payments, payroll, or vertical SaaS, or a business with complex money movement and a mix of SMB and enterprise customers; experience in the entertainment industry

 - Experience standing up a GTM engineering or AI-build function from scratch


Why Join Us

At Wrapbook, creativity meets technology — and not just in the product.

In addition to a competitive salary and all the benefits you can expect from a fast-growing technology company, you’ll get access to a team of creative problem solvers and the chance to see your contributions make large impacts. Benefits include:

 - Unlimited Paid Time Off

 - Work from anywhere in Canada and USA

 - Health and Dental benefits

 - Up to $1,500 USD/ $2,025 CAD towards IT set up for your home

 - Up to 2% matching RRSP / 401K

 - Learning and Development opportunities

 - Up to $50 USD/ $67.50 CAD towards Internet/Cell phone service

Our Pledge to Fostering an Inclusive and Safe Workplace:

Wrapbook pledges to be a harassment- and discrimination-free space for everyone, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, nationality, neurotype, personal appearance, political affiliation, professional background, race, religion, or sexual identity or orientation.

Apply Now

Have we got your attention? Submit your application today and a member of our Talent team will be in touch with you shortly!

title: VP Revenue Operations
description:
Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.



Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.



Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.



A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.



🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.



 💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.



🤝  We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.



💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.




ROLE OVERVIEW



Orbital is scaling through our Series B, and Revenue Operations is entering its next chapter. We've already defined the shape of the function: two Revenue Operations Managers, one focused on revenue-generation operations (Sales, Customer Success) and one focused on pipeline-generation operations (Marketing, Business Development), both reporting into this role. You'll inherit that structure and build on it.

You'll be responsible for creating the frameworks, insights, systems, and technology that bring together Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance into a cohesive growth engine, and for leading the team that executes on that vision day to day.

Reporting directly to the CRO, as a member of the commercial leadership team, you will combine strategic vision, operational execution, and people leadership, building the processes that drive predictability, the insights that guide decision-making, and the team and systems that enable our GTM organization to perform at its best.




WHY IT MATTERS

 - Lead the function. Take Orbital's Revenue Operations function to the next level by managing, developing, and scaling a team of two Revenue Operations Managers, while enhancing the frameworks, processes, and infrastructure that drive efficiency.

 - Clarity through data. Maintain a single source of truth for GTM performance.

 - Confidence at scale. Evolve the processes, operating rhythm, and forward-looking insights that give the CRO and leadership confidence in every decision. You'll enhance predictability and visibility, enabling Orbital to move boldly through its next stages of growth.

 - Drive alignment. Bring Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance together around shared goals and outcomes, and resolve the seams between your two managers' remits before they become friction.

 - Strategic partnership. Act as a trusted advisor to the CRO and leadership, shaping how we go to market.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Revenue Operations is a high-impact, well-led function, scaled to support rapid growth.

 - The two Revenue Operations Managers are clear on ownership, well supported, and growing in their roles.

 - GTM teams are enabled with the data, tools, and insight they need to succeed.

 - Leadership has clarity and predictability in revenue performance.

 - RevOps operates as an AI-native function, not just a function that uses AI tools.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Team Leadership

 - Manage and develop the two Revenue Operations Managers (RevGen and PipeGen), including regular 1:1s, coaching, and career growth

 - Own hiring plans and grow the RevOps team as Orbital scales

 - Set clear ownership across the seam between revenue-generation operations and pipeline-generation operations (for example: lead routing versus opportunity stage definitions, funnel attribution versus forecasting), and adjudicate where ownership is unclear

 - Own ramp for new GTM hires on RevOps systems and process, so new AEs, CSMs, and marketers are productive in HubSpot and the wider stack from day one

 - Own a recurring GTM alignment rhythm (for example, a pipeline or forecast review) that keeps Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance moving toward shared goals

GTM Strategy, Systems, and Stack

 - Own vendor selection, budget, and roadmap for the GTM tech stack (HubSpot, Apollo, Jiminny, Clay, Nook, and future AI-powered tools), setting direction that the RevOps Managers execute against

 - Ensure the team resolves system issues, inefficiencies, and data gaps proactively rather than reactively

 - Champion AI as a structural lever for how RevOps gets done, directing your managers' AI-native workstreams (deal inspection and forecasting AI for RevGen, enrichment and scoring AI for PipeGen) so they compound into one coherent, AI-fluent GTM engine

Territory, Capacity, and Compensation Planning

 - Own territory design and capacity planning across the Sales and Customer Success organizations, balancing opportunity, workload, and growth targets, and revisiting and rebalancing coverage as the team scales rather than leaving this to ad hoc adjustment

 - Set the methodology for how territories and quotas are built each planning cycle, and partner with Finance on compensation plan design and policy

Sales Process, Methodology & Deal Desk

 - Own the sales qualification methodology (for example, MEDDPICC or equivalent) and make sure it shows up consistently in HubSpot, not just in a deck

 - Define opportunity stage definitions and exit criteria in partnership with the RevGen Manager

 - Own the deal desk function: pricing and discounting approvals for non-standard deals, reviewed against a clear discounting policy so terms stay consistent across reps

 - Own contract structuring for non-standard commercial terms (multi-year deals, custom payment schedules, bundling), coordinating sign-off across Sales, Finance, and Legal, and track exceptions granted outside standard policy so terms do not quietly drift over time

Pipeline Generation Process & Funnel Definitions

 - Own the lead qualification methodology (MQL/SQL definitions or equivalent) and make sure it shows up consistently in HubSpot, not just in a deck

 - Define MQL/SQL stage definitions and exit criteria in partnership with the PipeGen Manager

 - Own multi-touch attribution methodology across marketing and BD channels, so channel and campaign performance can be trusted

 - Own lead scoring model governance (criteria, weighting, and routing thresholds), coordinating with Marketing and BD leadership as the funnel evolves

Retention, Expansion, and Account Health

 - Own retention and expansion metrics (NRR, GRR, churn, and expansion pipeline) as a core RevOps output, not an afterthought bolted onto Sales reporting

 - Partner with Customer Success leadership on renewal forecasting, account health scoring, and book re-balancing as the CS team grows

 - Ensure renewal and expansion motions are as well instrumented in HubSpot as new business pipeline

Reporting, Forecasting, and Insight

 - Own the definitions and data model behind GTM performance (pipeline, funnel, bookings, conversion, retention, and forecasting), so there is one trusted source of truth that the Managers report against

 - Own forecasting methodology and pipeline reporting delivered to the CRO and leadership

 - Translate data into strategic recommendations, not just dashboards




ABOUT YOU

You have built, scaled, and led Revenue Operations before, from Series A/B to C and beyond, and you know what great looks like. Critically, you have managed other RevOps professionals, not just processes. You are analytical, commercially minded, and comfortable working across functions to drive alignment and performance.

Experience you'll bring:

 - 8+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, with a proven track record of scaling B2B SaaS companies from Series A/B to C and beyond

 - Direct people management experience, having managed and developed RevOps, Sales Ops, or Marketing Ops professionals

 - Strong business and financial acumen

 - Data and analytical proficiency, with the ability to translate insights into strategic decisions and operational improvements

 - Hands-on expertise with key RevOps tech (HubSpot in particular), combined with the technical aptitude to evaluate and implement new tools

 - Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance leadership

 - A curious, AI-first mindset, eager to leverage automation and innovative approaches to create scale, and able to direct others in doing the same

How you work:

 - You think big about the future of RevOps and tackle the toughest challenges first, creating clarity and momentum in fast-scaling environments

 - You empower your team and the wider GTM organization with the tools, systems, and clarity they need to succeed

 - Structured, analytical, and data-driven, using evidence-based debate to reach decisions quickly rather than slowly

 - An exceptional communicator and leader who builds trust, alignment, and accountability across teams, including with the managers who report to you

 - Collaborative, egoless, and outcome-focused, always putting the success of the team and business first




WHY YOU'LL LOVE IT HERE

 - You'll join a startup at an exciting inflection point, with real influence at the leadership table from day one.

 - You'll tackle the kind of business challenges that make this a genuinely career-defining role.

 - You'll be part of a collaborative, highly ambitious and friendly culture where curiosity and innovation are celebrated.




BENEFITS 🌟

 - Compensation: We offer a competitive starting salary in the range of $260,000-$300,000, depending on experience. We share salary ranges upfront to build trust, reduce bias, and support an inclusive process, even as we continue developing our internal pay structures.

 - We believe in flexibility, but we're also big on in-person collaboration. This role is based in our New York office with minimum two days a week, with additional time in as needed for things like all-hands, interviews, or team sessions. It's about being present when it matters, and balancing autonomy with impact.

 - 401k match and equity options in a fast-growing start-up.

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents.

 - Rest and Recharge: 20 days paid holiday (plus public holidays), so you can rest, recharge, and take care of what matters most to you.

 - Generous parental leave policy designed to support all parents and caregivers in balancing family and work life, in addition to any state-mandated paid family leave entitlements.

 - Professional equipment and personal development budget along with training opportunities to learn and develop your skills.

 - Pre-tax commuter benefits to help you get to and from the office.

 - We're in the process of building an inclusive, welcoming culture where everyone feels seen and valued. Expect regular team off-sites, shared lunches, and social events, with something for everyone.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.



💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially welcome applications from people who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, or if the right role isn’t listed yet, we’d still love to hear from you.



💰 This hiring range is a reasonable estimate of the base pay range for this position at the time of posting. Pay is based on several factors, which may include job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and business requirements.



Everyone who works with Orbital goes through background screening before they start. It's part of how we keep Orbital secure, for the people who work here and for the client information we're trusted with.

GTM ENGINEER - CX @ CLAY

We're looking for someone to focus on elevating our post-sale workflows ; building automations that help prevent churn and identify expansion opportunities. You'll sit at the intersection of GTM Engineering and the CX org, partnering closely with Product Support and Growth Strategy to turn customer data into proactive, measurable action. Strong candidates will be builders who with a strong understanding of the CX org motion: how GSMs, CSMs, and support teams operate and what data they need to be effective. You will operate with high agency but ground yourself in what your stakeholders need to be successful.


What You'll Do

 - Build and own post-sale workflow automations like health scoring, churn signal detection, expansion opportunity identification, and proactive customer outreach triggers

 - Partner closely with Growth Strategy, Forward Deployed Engineering and Product Support to translate business needs into automation requirements and iterate based on feedback

 - Build tooling that surfaces the right customer context for GSMs at the right moment; before QBRs, during renewals, and ahead of expansion conversations

 - Push the limits of Clay and extend our platform into new use cases, feed our product team innovative ideas, dogfood new features and ; act as a practitioner evangelist of Clay infrastructure and GTM Engineering

 - Partner deeply with GTM leaders and frontline teams to understand how our revenue motion works today and where it breaks

 - Own projects end-to-end, from discovery and prototyping through rollout, adoption, and iteration; identify opportunities to automate, augment, or redesign workflows using AI, data, and better systems design

 - Design systems that improve speed, visibility, data quality, and execution across the funnel; connect systems through APIs, webhooks, integrations, and automation layers so information moves cleanly across the stack

 - Measure performance, adoption, and business impact of what you build, then improve it over time

 - Act as an internal thought partner on the future of AI-native GTM systems

What You'll Bring

 - At least 6-10 years working in a combination of RevOps, GTM Engineering or other similar applied technical discipline with

 - At least 3 years in RevOps/Sales Ops or GTM Engineering or equivalent

 - Experience building, developing or connecting core systems like Salesforce and adjacent GTM systems including hands on experience with CS tooling such as Gainsight, Vitally, or ChurnZero

 - Proven ability to build and problem solve with methods incorporating Python, JavaScript, SQL, or TypeScript; we pull our own data on this team

 - Track record of deploying and building AI-powered internal tools, automations, or agentic workflows

 - Experience using data warehouses, BI tools, or event-driven systems

 - Executive presence -- you communicate concisely and confidently even about technical topics with non technical people while simultaneously communicating business requirements to technical audiences

 - Proven ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and fluid hypergrowth environments -- you not only embrace change bur drive it

 - Experience building in Clay as a primary workflow or enrichment layer is not required but is highly preferred (successful candidates with no experience in Clay will show increasing proficiency throughout the interview process)

 - Bonus points for experience in analytics engineering, data science and /or programming languages

title: Staff GTM Engineer
description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



At 1Password, we want our Go-To-Market teams to have the best tools, data, and AI available. We're looking for a Staff GTM Engineer to join Revenue Operations and own the architecture, development, and operation of the AI applications, agents, and data pipelines across our sales, marketing, and customer success stack.

This is a hands-on, cross-functional engineering role. You'll write and ship production code, set the technical direction for AI in GTM, and bring engineering rigor to the work: architecture reviews, testing, CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery), and observability. You'll work closely with operations, systems, analytics, engineering, and security teams to turn ideas into reliable services that help revenue teams work faster and smarter.



Reporting into the Senior Director, GTM Engineering, this role is a remote opportunity within Canada and the USA.



How we’re using AI today

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.



Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.



What we're looking for:

• Bring 6 or more years of engineering experience, including ownership of production tools from initial design through deployment and ongoing operation.

• Work directly with GTM workflows and systems such as Salesforce, Clay, HubSpot, Outreach, Gong, and Gainsight, including their application programming interfaces (APIs) and data models.

• Build production agentic applications using prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases, tool calling, evaluation frameworks, and observability.

• Translate business goals and pain points into clear technical requirements, explain tradeoffs in plain language, and collaborate effectively with non-technical GTM leaders and cross-functional partners.

• Write clean, tested, maintainable code and apply strong engineering practices, including version control, code review, debugging, and consistent coding standards.

• Deploy and operate production services on Amazon Web Services (AWS) or Google Cloud Platform (GCP), using containers or serverless infrastructure, infrastructure as code, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), monitoring, and alerting.

• Use Structured Query Language (SQL) and data modeling to build reliable data pipelines between systems.



What you can expect:

 - Ship AI into the revenue workflow: Design, build, and run production agents and services for lead scoring, enrichment, routing, summarization, and personalized outreach across GTM systems.

 - Own the GTM technical roadmap: Partner with RevOps and GTM leaders to find and prioritize the use cases worth building, and make the build vs. buy and architecture calls behind them

 - Build the platform others build on: Create shared APIs, integrations, and data pipelines that connect revenue systems, so each new use case ships faster than the last

 - Make AI measurable and safe to change: Put evaluations, monitoring, and staged rollouts around every AI workflow, and partner with Security and IT to protect customer data

 - Set the engineering bar for GTM: Establish standards for code review, linting, testing, CI/CD, and documentation. Mentor engineers and technical operators

 - Run what you build: Join the on-call rotation for your systems and lead incident response and follow-up fixes





USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $139,000 USD and $202,000 USD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $124,000 CAD and $180,000 CAD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.


Our approach to work
We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement.

For all roles, occasional travel may be required. This includes things like: department-wide offsites, quarterly department meetings and periodic customer events. These events are typically held in varying locations across Canada, USA and/or EMEA. In leadership roles, you can expect to travel once per month on average.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto. 


What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer: 

Health and wellbeing
👶 Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
🩺 Competitive health benefits
🏝 Generous PTO policy 

 Growth and future 
📈 RSU program for most employees
💸 Retirement matching program
🔑 Free 1Password account

Community 
🤝 Paid volunteer days 
🏆 Peer-to-peer recognition through Bonusly
🌎 Remote-first work environment
*Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.



You belong here.



1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Be yourself, find your people and share the things you love.



Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at nextbit@agilebits.com and we’ll work to meet your needs.



Remote work is a part of our DNA. Given that our company was founded remotely in 2005, we can safely say we're experts at building remote culture. That said, remote work at 1Password does mean working from your home country. If you've got questions or concerns about this, your talent partner would be happy to address them with you.



Successful applicants will be required to complete a background check that may consist of prior employment verification, reference checks, education confirmation, criminal background, publicly available social media, credit history, or other information, as permitted by local law.



1Password uses artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies, including natural language processing and predictive analytics, to assist in the initial screening of employment applications and improve our recruitment process. See here https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf for the latest third party bias audit information. If you prefer not to have your application assessed using AI/ML features, you may opt out by completing this form https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/1password/automation-notice. For additional information see our Candidate Privacy Notice https://1password.com/files/candidate-privacy-notice.pdf.

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.



What we're looking for:

• 8+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, or sales strategy and operations within Business-to-Business (B2B) software, including 3+ years leading teams.

• Deep experience with sales forecasting, pipeline management, sales process, and operating rhythms across multiple segments.

• Experience leading annual planning, territory design, quota setting, and in-year adjustments.

• Experience supporting sales organizations across multiple regions, including Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA).

• Ability to build trusted relationships with senior Sales leaders, communicate clearly, and influence decisions using sound judgment and data.

• Experience hiring, developing, and coaching strong sales or revenue operations leaders.

• Experience using Salesforce and artificial intelligence (AI) to improve forecasting, pipeline management, or sales productivity.



What you can expect:

• Partner with Sales leaders to set quarterly priorities, align hiring plans and trade-offs, and create recovery plans when teams fall behind.

• Establish consistent global standards for forecast calls, pipeline reviews, and quarterly business reviews.

• Develop independent forecasts for each team, lead large-deal reviews, and turn insights into clear decisions.

• Improve sales productivity through stronger coverage, faster ramping, and effective support from solution engineering and Privileged Access specialists.

• Lead the use of AI in forecasting and pipeline work, helping managers reinvest time saved into selling and coaching.

• Run annual planning with Sales Strategy and Planning and Enablement so that teams begin each year with clear territories and quotas.

• Lead and develop a high-performing global field sales operations team.





USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $187,000 USD and $257,000 USD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $160,000 CAD and $220,000 CAD. This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.


Our approach to work
We recognize the power of both in person collaboration and remote work. Some roles are designated as remote-first, with an expectation that individuals work from their homes majority of the time, while others are designated as in-office roles, with an expectation of being on-site on a regular basis. We recognize that certain roles benefit from regular, in-person connection to support collaboration, team cohesion, and customer engagement.

For all roles, occasional travel may be required. This includes things like: department-wide offsites, quarterly department meetings and periodic customer events. These events are typically held in varying locations across Canada, USA and/or EMEA. In leadership roles, you can expect to travel once per month on average.

Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto. 


What we offer
We believe in working hard, and rewarding that hard work through our benefits. While not an exhaustive list, here is a glance at what we currently offer:

*Some roles in our GTM team are currently being hired for in-person hybrid work in Toronto and Austin. These roles will specify on the posting.



You belong here.



1Password is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect.
