title: Business Systems Analyst, GTM Systems
description:
ABOUT US

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry.

More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it.

We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next.

You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale.

This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates.

You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan.

You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct.

Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Carry multi-quarter programs

 - Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption.

 - Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs.

 - Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets.

Own what gets specified and what ships

 - Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation.

 - Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off.

 - Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build.

Protect revenue data integrity

 - Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them.

 - Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions.

 - Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

In your first 6–12 months, you might:

 - Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field.

 - Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale.

 - Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation.

 - Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against.

 - Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING


SYSTEMS AND DOMAIN DEPTH

 - Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout.

 - Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene.

 - Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes.

 - Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code.


PROGRAM LEADERSHIP

 - Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day.

 - Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release.

 - Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality.

 - Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative.


JUDGMENT AND COMMUNICATION

 - One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec.

 - Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket.

 - AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way.

 - Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it.


NICE TO HAVE'S

None of these is a screen; any one makes you useful faster.

 - You've owned a core Salesforce object domain — Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity — through a full redesign.

 - You've traced a Salesforce field into a usage record into a provisioning step, and seen what broke downstream when it moved.

 - You've worked with cloud marketplace operations — AWS or GCP private offers, co-sell, entitlement mapping, metering, and the failure modes when they break.

 - You've worked with usage-based billing systems such as Metronome, Orb, or similar, and CRM↔billing identity reconciliation.

 - You have LangChain or LangGraph experience, or you're excited to learn it here from the people who build it.




COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.




BENEFITS

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a GTM Systems Engineer to design, build, and scale the technical infrastructure behind our go-to-market engine.

You’ll own the design and implementation of GTM systems and integrations, connecting our CRM, marketing automation, sales tools, finance and product systems, and data warehouse. You’ll turn manual processes into reliable, automated workflows and help teams trust the data behind the sales funnel.

You’ll partner with Revenue Operations and Sales Operations on business processes, and with Finance, Product, Data Engineering, and IT on connected systems and data. This is a hands-on builder role for a systems thinker who can design and ship technical solutions, make sound architectural decisions, communicate tradeoffs, and own problems end to end in a fast-moving environment.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Build and connect the GTM stack

 - Architect and build applications, automations, and integrations across the GTM stack, including Salesforce, CPQ, marketing automation, and sales tools.

 - Design, build, and own integrations and data flows between GTM systems, the finance and product technology stacks, and the data warehouse using APIs, webhooks, and reverse ETL.

 - Partner with Sales Operations to build and maintain automations for data hygiene, pipeline management, deal desk processes, and other lead-to-cash workflows.

 - Prototype and productionize AI-assisted and agent-based workflows that reduce manual work or surface timely account signals, with appropriate human review.

Create reliable data and systems

 - Design and implement data models, deduplication, validation rules, and monitoring to improve data integrity across systems.

 - Build the data flows and infrastructure that power reporting, dashboards, and forecasting in partnership with Revenue Operations and Data Engineering.

 - Build reliable, maintainable solutions using appropriate testing, deployment and release practices, monitoring, documentation, and change management. Troubleshoot integrations and maintain them as connected systems change.

 - Build or implement solutions to close gaps in the GTM stack, and evaluate and retire tools as the business scales.

Partner across the business

 - Work with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Finance, Product, IT, and Data Engineering to understand needs and build effective solutions.

 - Communicate technical concepts, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Prioritize and deliver engineering initiatives and enhancements while resolving issues in production systems.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 8+ years of experience building and integrating business or GTM systems, including in Business Systems, GTM Engineering, Revenue Operations, or a technical Sales or Marketing Operations role at a high-growth company.

 - Deep hands-on experience building and customizing Salesforce solutions, including applications, objects, flows, permissions, and integrations.

 - Skills in Apex, Lightning components, Salesforce APIs, SOAP- or REST-based web services, and SOQL.

 - Strong SQL skills and experience working with a data warehouse.

 - Experience with Workato, Zapier, MuleSoft, Boomi, or another integration platform.

 - Experience with CPQ and end-to-end lead-to-cash flows and integrations.

 - Hands-on experience building AI-powered or agent-based workflows to solve practical business problems.

 - A systems-thinking mindset: you design for scale, document your work, and care about clean data.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, sound judgment in prioritizing competing work, and clear communication across teams.

 - Comfort in a high-intensity, high-autonomy environment and a desire to own problems end to end.
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with Snowflake or BigQuery.

 - Experience building and maintaining billing systems.

 - Scripting experience in Python or JavaScript.




HOW WE’LL MEASURE SUCCESS

Over the first 6–12 months, success could include:

 - High-priority Sales Operations and lead-to-cash workflows are automated or simplified, reducing manual work.

 - Critical integrations are documented, monitored, and maintained, with clear ownership and a path for resolving failures.

 - Revenue Operations and Data Engineering partners see agreed-upon improvements in data quality and confidence in funnel reporting.

 - AI-assisted workflows help GTM teams act on useful signals or spend less time on manual tasks.

 - Cross-functional partners understand the solutions built and how they address business needs.




COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.




BENEFITS

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

title: RevOps Manager
description:
About Ryft

 

Ryft is a regulated payment facilitator and authorised payment institution building the infrastructure layer for modern commerce platforms.

We enable marketplaces, SaaS platforms and multi-party ecosystems to embed and monetise payments natively. Our technology handles onboarding, compliance, orchestration, split payments and revenue sharing, allowing our partners to focus on growth while we manage complexity.

 

We are now entering the next phase of scale, expanding into new verticals and building a category-defining embedded payments platform.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to build the RevOps function at Ryft from scratch. This is our first RevOps hire, reporting into [Commercial Director / commercial leadership], and you'll own the entire revenue engine end-to-end — the systems, the data, and the reporting the commercial team runs on.

There is no function to inherit. You'll be doing the work as well as designing it: getting HubSpot into a state we can trust, building the forecasting and pipeline visibility leadership needs, and putting the operating rhythm in place that keeps the commercial motion honest. As the team and function grow, this role grows with it.




YOU WILL...



Get the foundations right

• Audit and architect the GTM tech stack, establishing HubSpot as the single source of truth for Sales, Marketing and Customer Success

• Define the commercial motion end to end — stages, ownership, what moves a deal forward — and the small set of fields it depends on

• Make sure leads are picked up and worked, with nothing dropped between inbound and owned pipeline



Build visibility and forecasting

• Stand up a forecasting process built on pipeline health, accurate enough to plan and raise against

• Build the dashboards that give the commercial team and leadership one shared, trusted view of the funnel

• Implement attribution models that show leadership what's actually driving pipeline



Sharpen how we operate

• Put operating cadences in place — the regular reviews that keep the motion honest

• Analyse conversion across the funnel, find where deals stall, and fix it through process, tooling or training

• Sharpen our view of ideal customer profile so effort concentrates where it converts



Extend the data layer

• Build and manage the outbound data layer — signal sourcing and enrichment — to operationalise high-performing outbound plays using tools like Clay



Cross-functional

• Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success and Finance to keep planning, reporting and execution aligned

• Feed data-driven insight back into commercial strategy and leadership decisions




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR



Experience

• 3+ years in RevOps or Sales Ops within B2B SaaS, ideally as first or sole operator in a high-growth startup

• Hands-on CRM architecture experience — HubSpot expertise strongly preferred

• Experience building forecasting, reporting or attribution frameworks from a messy or early-stage starting point

• Experience with modern GTM tooling (e.g. Clay) for outbound data and enrichment



Skills that will help you succeed

• A builder mindset — you want to build the function, not inherit and maintain one

• Comfortable being the person in the CRM and the data, not just directing others

• Strong analytical communicator who can turn messy datasets into clear, executive-ready narratives

• Commercially fluent — you understand pipeline, conversion and the economics of the sales motion

• Startup temperament — thrives with ambiguity, ships a usable version early, iterates

• Payments or fintech experience is a strong advantage, though builder instinct matters more than sector background

Please note these are not all absolute requirements. We value attitude and cultural fit as much as experience, so if you don't match all of the above but are interested in the role, please don't hesitate to apply.

title: GTM Engineer
description:
COMPETENCIES

You are an applied AI engineer whose product is the revenue engine. You find where the customer lifecycle can work better and ship production-grade agentic workflow, LLM pipelines and integrations that make each process best in class for reps, CSMs and marketers. You operate independently and own each build end to end: architecture, prototype, evals, deployment and observability. You spar on solution design with the team, then ship.

We care more about what you have shipped than where you studied. If you have built something real, show us.

Must-haves

 - You have shipped AI systems GTM teams use daily. Agents, workflows or integrations used by sales, CS or marketing that moved a number.

 - Strong integration skills in JavaScript or TypeScript. You’re comfortable building and running integration services. Working with APIs and webhooks, handling auth, rate limits and errors, and shipping tested code.

 - Hands-on Salesforce or equivalent, declarative and code. Declarative: object model, Flows, validation rules, permission sets, record types. Code: Apex triggers and classes, SOQL and SOSL, Lightning Web Components, Platform Events and Change Data Capture, REST and Bulk APIs, SFDX deployments.

 - Applied AI engineering. You build with LLM APIs, not just chat interfaces, and can show the skills listed below in real work.

 - You understand the revenue engine. Experience in RevOps, GTM Systems, growth or a GTM engineering agency in B2B SaaS. You know how pipeline, renewals and expansion actually work.

 - Data quality fundamentals. SQL, CRM data models, deduplication, enrichment waterfalls and data quality at scale.

 - GTM data stack. Clay, n8n, Make + warehouse and reverse ETL experience.

 - Production mindset. You ship fast and build things others can maintain: logged, monitored, documented.

 - Clear communicator. You can sit with a top rep, find the work that shouldn't exist, and explain the fix in plain words.

Nice-to-haves

 - Experience with a customer platform or CSM tool (Planhat, Gainsight, ChurnZero), or HubSpot alongside Salesforce.

 - Salesforce certifications such as Platform Developer I or II, or Platform App Builder.

 - Side projects, open-source tools, public write-ups or a GitHub that shows you build for fun.

 - Founder, agency or early-stage startup experience.


TRAJECTORY

You’ll own each build end to end, from architecture and prototype through evals, deployment and observability. Here’s what that looks like:

 - Agentic GTM workflows: Design and ship AI agents and workflows that optimise productivity: account research, signal detection, enrichment, call and email analysis, personalised outreach, renewal and expansion plays.

 - Planhat on Planhat: Run our own GTM on our own platform. Build with Planhat's AI, automations and APIs, and feed what you learn straight back to Product as a power user.

 - Signals and data: Turn product usage, intent, firmographic and conversation data into scores and triggers that route the right account to the right person at the right time.

 - Integrations: Connect tools that don't talk natively. Build the webhooks, MCP connection and transformations that keep data clean across the stack.

 - Build vs buy: Run tight pilots on new GTM and AI tools, measure fit and ROI, and make a clear call.

 - Enablement: Document what you build, teach teams to use it with confidence, and raise how the whole company builds with AI.


DEFINITION OF SUCCESS

Success is measured in outcomes: productivity gains, pipeline acceleration, data quality and adoption of what you ship.

title: Sales Operations Analyst
description:
WHO WE ARE

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells https://blog.roboflow.com/cancer-research-computer-vision/ to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety https://blog.roboflow.com/preventing-accidents-on-construction-sites-with-computer-vision/, digitizing floor plans https://blog.roboflow.com/floor-plan-analysis-computer-vision/, preserving coral reef populations https://blog.roboflow.com/reefos-supercharging-coral-reef-restoration-with-ai/, guiding drone flight https://blog.roboflow.com/georeferencing-drone-videos/, and much more https://roboflow.com/templates.

Our team is small relative to our impact, and we believe our user success is our success (not the inverse). A team member summarized: “Roboflow is a company full of giant brains and tiny egos.” We find software has a multiplier effect on all roles (not only product and engineering), so Roboflow employs developers across the company in design, sales, customer support, marketing, and beyond.

We’re supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Google Ventures, Y Combinator, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

We’re hiring a Sales Operations Analyst to run the day-to-day operating rhythm of our revenue team and to stand up our deal desk, reporting into the Revenue Operations lead and working closely with sales leadership, finance, and our GTM Systems Engineer. Revenue Operations owns the operating system for go-to-market at Roboflow: how pipeline is measured, how the forecast is built, how territory and quota are set, and whether the numbers can be trusted. This role is the analytical and commercial half of that mandate. You’ll own the analysis leadership makes decisions from, and you’ll be the person reps come to when a deal needs to be structured, priced, and approved.

You’ll work alongside a GTM Systems Engineer who builds and maintains the systems themselves. Where they own how Salesforce works, you own what the numbers mean and how a deal gets done. Our motion is land-and-expand into enterprise manufacturing with packaged site licenses and a fast-growing first-land play, so deal structuring here is real work with real leverage, and the forecast has several distinct models underneath it.

 - Own day-to-day deal desk duties: guide reps on deal structure and packaging, run pricing and discount approvals, handle non-standard terms, and drive the path from quote to signed order form, including cloud marketplace transactions

 - Maintain pricing and packaging guardrails with Finance and sales leadership, including approval thresholds, discount bands, and the guidance reps use to size a site license or a proof of value

 - Contribute to the weekly and monthly forecast process: assemble the forecast, track submitted forecast against actuals, and surface slip, drift, and coverage gaps by segment

 - Own the recurring analysis leadership decides from, including pipeline generation, conversion by stage and segment, win/loss, sales cycle, and team performance

 - Support territory, coverage, and quota planning with account distribution, whitespace, capacity math, and attainment tracking

 - Steward KPI definitions so a number means the same thing in every meeting, dashboard, and report, and be the person who can explain any of them on the spot

 - Run the data quality cadence with reps: publish the cleanup views, work each list down with its owner, and escalate recurring problems for a systems fix

 - Support the variable compensation program through attainment reporting, plan mechanics, and the data quality behind both


WHO YOU ARE

You are a commercially minded analyst, equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and in the middle of a live deal, who wants to be an important part of an exceptional team that focuses on using Roboflow's computer vision tools to impact and improve every industry. You have high agency and a bias toward action.

Required Skills:

 - 3+ years in sales operations, revenue operations, deal desk, or a sales-facing analytics role at a B2B software company

 - Strong analytical skills: you can build and defend a model in a spreadsheet, and you write SQL or will pick it up quickly

 - Hands-on Salesforce experience as a power user, including reports, dashboards, pipeline inspection, and opportunity and forecast data

 - Practical understanding of GTM mechanics: pipeline stages, forecast categories, coverage, win rates, territory and quota concepts

title: GTM Engineer
description:
THE ROLE


Growth owns the systems that power our go-to-market motion: our CRM, connected to enrichment, sales engagement, outbound agents, lifecycle, routing, visitor intelligence and paid, with GTM OS, our internal platform, tying them together. We are hiring a GTM Engineer to run that motion and build the agents and data layer it depends on.



Nash builds the autonomic logistics platform: a system that senses what is happening across a network, decides what to do about it and adjusts as the results come back, without waiting to be told. Our go-to-market should run the same way. A signal comes in, an agent decides what to do with it, the rep gets the account ready to work, and every outcome writes back so the next decision is better than the last.



Most of the pieces exist. GTM OS is in production, the agents run, the stack is connected. Your job is to turn them into one reliable engine that produces pipeline, hold it to a production bar, then decide what it does next.



WHAT YOU'LL DO


 - Build and run the AI agents that work across our GTM motion: account research, signal qualification, message construction, routing and reply handling, from design through evals, rollout and the monitoring that keeps them honest

 - Build the infrastructure to run paid and ABM as one system: audiences generated from the CRM, campaigns launched and paused by rules you write, engagement flowing back into the agents, and spend tied to accounts worked and pipeline created

 - Own the account context layer every agent and campaign is grounded in: entity resolution, evidence typing, freshness and provenance, and the segment, industry, region and product rules that define our market

 - Build on GTM OS, our internal platform, and make what it can do available to sales and marketing inside the tools they already use

 - Be the technical owner of our go-to-market systems, the CRM and everything connected to it, from the data model and routing logic to the integrations and automations that keep the whole stack current and consistent

 - Own sending infrastructure and deliverability: domain strategy, warming, suppression and sender reputation across every program that sends

 - Hold the production bar: evals, observability, permissions and auditability, so the system reports its own failures before a rep finds them

 - Be measured on what the motion produces: reply and meeting rates, pipeline and revenue, cost per account worked. Agent reliability and data quality are how you get there
   
   

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - A go-to-market record: outbound, paid, ABM or lifecycle programs you ran, with the pipeline they produced and the systems you built to run them

 - Software you shipped and kept running: a service, agent or pipeline in production that other people depended on, with something we can look at

 - Outbound that scales and still reads like a person: sequences triggered by something that just changed for the buyer and tied to what we sell, reply rates to show for them, and the judgment to pull apart a message that is not landing

 - Paid media fluency: you have run budgets and built audiences, and you know which decisions should stay with a person

 - Hands-on experience applying AI to go-to-market systems: agents, LLM-based automation, MCP-style integrations, and the evals that tell you whether any of it works

 - Fluency in Python or TypeScript, and daily work with Claude Code, Cursor or equivalent, with specific opinions about where the tooling fails

 - Integration experience: you have built and debugged integrations through APIs and understand auth, rate limits, sync direction and failure modes

 - Salesforce as a developer: the data model, the API, and Apex, or the track record to pick it up fast

 - Data fluency: SQL, warehouse concepts, and the habit of tracing a data quality issue from source to destination

 - You can turn a vague request into scoped work and explain the tradeoffs


HOW TO APPLY


Send us your resume, links to things you have built and kept running (a repo, a live service, an agent, a sequence with its results), and a short note on the system or motion you are most proud of and why. If you would rather skip the cover letter, send a Loom walking us through a piece of work, or a Replit prototype of a GTM agent you would build for Nash. Both are very much encouraged.



Want to grab our attention and bypass the recruiting platform? Record a video introducing yourself at testimonials.nash.ai http://testimonials.nash.ai with code JOIN-NASH. Your application notifies us in Slack the moment it lands, and we get some much needed testing coverage on our latest Claude build :)




More about Nash http://Nash.AI


NASH IS THE PLATFORM THAT POWERS MODERN LOGISTICS.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.




WHAT YOU’LL LOVE ABOUT US

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

title: GTM Engineer
description:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.

Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

Our ambition is to put AI capability in every worker’s hands. Apprenticeships got us started: we’ve trained over a third of the UK’s data and AI apprentices, worked with a third of the FTSE 100, and generated £2bn+ in verified ROI. Now Mastry, our new adaptive learning platform, takes that further, guiding a company’s AI workforce transformation from start to finish. Mae, our AI guide inside Mastry, is a real-time AI agent that thinks, speaks, listens and sees, working alongside the tools you already use, like Claude and Copilot.

We closed our latest fundraising round in April 2026, with $500m+ raised in total from VC partners including Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Schroders Capital and Lightspeed. With a $2.1bn valuation, we are Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn, and we are just getting started.

If you want to shape how the workforce wins in the AI era, come and join us.

What You’ll Do

 - Build AI workflow automation. Design, build and ship AI-powered workflows that remove manual GTM work; from lead research and CRM enrichment to call analysis, personalised outreach and lifecycle automation. Own builds end to end, from problem definition through deployment, monitoring and iteration.

 - Bridge gaps between systems. Find creative ways to connect tools that do not natively integrate. Build the webhooks, middleware, scripts and glue that keep data flowing cleanly between Salesforce and the rest of the stack.

 - Solve multi-departmental integration challenges. Work across the boundaries of Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Data and Finance to turn tangled, cross-functional processes into reliable, automated systems.

 - Prototype, test and scale. Test new ideas at small scale, measure what works, and scale the versions that deliver. Bring a bias to ship a working prototype over a perfect specification.

 - Build with AI as the default. Use LLMs, agentic workflows, MCP builds and evals as everyday tools. Ask “how would AI do this?” before reaching for headcount or manual effort.

 - Own reliability. Treat what you build as production systems: instrument them, monitor them, handle failure gracefully, and reduce risk across the GTM tech stack.

 - Evaluate and recommend. Run structured pilots of new tools, assess capability, integration fit, reliability and ROI, and make clear build-versus-buy recommendations.

 - Set the standard. Document what you build, enable GTM teams to adopt it with confidence, and mentor others in the team on building with AI and automation.

What You’ll Bring

 - Significant hands-on experience in RevOps, GTM Systems, or Sales Operations within enterprise technology, ideally in a structured qualification environment such as MEDDPICC. You understand the full GTM engine and you know what good looks like when real revenue depends on the systems you own.

 - Solid data and systems fundamentals. You understand CRM data models, object relationships, data quality and reporting architecture, and you design builds that keep data clean and trustworthy at scale.

 - A track record of building for internal GTM teams. Your strongest work is systems and workflows used every day by sales, marketing or CS teams inside a business, not only side projects, single-client builds or customer-facing pre-sales work.

 - A builder’s mindset on top of that foundation. You have built things, not just configured them. You can point to workflows, automations, integrations or tools you shipped that moved a real metric, ideally things nobody explicitly asked you to build.

 - You learn systems fast. You pick up unfamiliar platforms quickly and reason about how they fit together. You are comfortable reading API documentation, handling authentication, respecting rate limits, and parsing JSON when a native connector does not exist.

 - Fluency with AI as a build material. Hands-on experience using LLMs, agentic workflows, prompt design and evals to build systems you can trust in production, not just as an end user.

 - Comfort across low-code and code. You build with whatever fits the problem, from orchestration tools and Salesforce Flows through to scripting in Python, JavaScript, SOQL or SQL where it earns its place.

 - Cross-functional range. You can interview a top rep to find the manual work that should not exist, translate a business problem into a technical build, and explain the result in plain language.

 - Bias to ship, balanced with judgement. You move fast and decisively, and you build things others can maintain rather than sticky-plaster fixes.

 - Deep CRM knowledge. Strong hands-on Salesforce experience, or deep expertise in a comparable enterprise CRM. Certifications are welcome but experience matters more.

Beneficial, But Not Required

 - Experience with traditional GTM third-party tooling such as Gong, LeanData, Lusha, Cognism, Clay, Floqer, Zapier, Tableau, Snowflake, Guru, or equivalents.

 - Evidence of experimenting with AI beyond your day job, such as side projects or personal builds that show how you think.

How You’ll Work: Our Operating Principles

 - Solve for Customer Value. Define the customer problem and the value of solving it before you build.

 - Drivers, Not Passengers. Take ownership and accountability, and bring others with you.

 - Be Decisive, Even in Ambiguity. Speed is the strategy. Act with velocity over total certainty.

 - AI to Deliver Outcomes. AI is our engine, not an add-on.





Benefits

 - Time off: 27 days holiday (including 3 winter shutdown days) and bank holidays, plus 5 extra days off (1 life event, 2 volunteer days and 2 summer shutdown days).

 - Health and wellbeing: Bupa private medical insurance, a medical cash back plan, therapy through Spill and gym access through Wellhub.

 - Equity for all: we believe that when Multiverse wins, we all win, which is why every permanent employee receives share options.

 - Financial security: life insurance at 3x salary, a workplace pension with 4% contribution from us, Cycle to Work and a Tech Scheme.

 - Family support: enhanced maternity and paternity leave, adoption and shared parental leave, paid leave after pregnancy loss, and a workplace nursery scheme.

 - Hybrid working: 3 days a week in the office - except for Coaches & Instructors who come into the office 1 day per month. Plus 10 days a year to work from anywhere.

 - Work perks: quarterly team socials, company-wide events, happy hours, lunch delivered to the office once a week, fully stocked snack bar and a drinks fridge!


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here https://www.multiverse.io/en-GB/our-policies/equality-diversity-and-inclusion-policy.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy https://cdn.sanity.io/files/6y1mknvo/prod-20240319/50283d0600920c5f1e02cf44e54c0f1534c74e61.pdf, our Prevent Policy  https://cdn.sanity.io/files/6y1mknvo/prod-20240319/35a5defca7346bb1c212250867754b0a7ae5b478.pdfand all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS). 

For roles that will involve a Regulated Activity, successful applicants must also undergo an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children’s Barred List check and a Prohibition Order check. Roles involving Regulated Activity may interact with vulnerable groups, therefore are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 meaning applicants are required to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings.

Providing false information is an offence and could result in the application being rejected or summary dismissal if the applicant has been selected, and possible referral to the police and the DBS.

title: Head of GTM Strategy & Ops - Global Partnerships
description:
ABOUT US:

Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI.


THE ROLE

Partnerships are a core growth motion at Fireworks, from cloud co-sell and marketplace motions to system integrators and technology partners. The Head of GTM Strategy & Ops - Global Partnerships is the business partner and strategic thought partner to the VP of Partnerships and the partnerships leadership team. You turn partner strategy into measurable pipeline stages, a reliable weekly operating cadence, and planning and capacity decisions.

You will sit inside the Sales Strategy & Analytics team and work every day with partnerships leadership, partner managers, direct sellers and Finance. You will make partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline visible and trustworthy, run the partner forecast and pipeline reviews, and set the rules that keep partners and direct sellers working together.

This is a builder role in a fast-moving startup. Some tooling and reporting exist, much of the operating system around them does not, and priorities change quickly. The right candidate is comfortable defining the process, doing the analysis themselves, and working with partnerships, sales, finance and engineering teams to get it adopted. Fireworks sells on consumption and hybrid commit + usage models, so experience with usage-based revenue is a strong plus.


RESPONSIBILITIES


BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP & STRATEGY

 - Act as strategic thought partner to the VP of Partnerships on where to focus, where to invest and what to stop across partner motions.

 - Help segment and tier partners, and translate partner strategy into joint plans, priorities and measurable goals.

 - Run the weekly, monthly and quarterly business reviews for Partnerships, with clear decisions, owners and deadlines.

 - Prepare executive and board-ready updates on the partner flywheel with the VP of Partnerships.


PARTNER PIPELINE, FORECAST & ANALYTICS

 - Define stage progression, sourced versus influenced attribution and credit rules for partner pipeline with Sales, RevOps and Finance.

 - Run the partner pipeline and forecast review: inspect deals, pressure-test commits and surface risk early.

 - Own the partner funnel analytics (stage conversion, win rate, sourced versus influenced split), ready for QBRs.

 - Define requirements for partner dashboards, forecasting views and alerts with GTM Analytics and GTM Engineering, and push for automation of weekly reporting.


PLANNING, TARGETS & CAPACITY

 - Drive partner annual and in-year planning with Partnerships leadership, Sales and Finance.

 - Set partner pipeline and revenue targets in alignment with the VP of Partnerships and sales leadership.

 - Model partner team capacity and give hiring recommendations that tie headcount to pipeline and revenue goals.

 - Work with Incentive Strategy on how partner contribution is credited and rewarded.


PARTNER OPERATIONS & PROCESSES

 - Define rules of engagement between partners and direct sellers, including account ownership, deal credit and conflict resolution.

 - Build and maintain co-sell and referral processes, deal registration and CRM hygiene for partner data.

 - Partner with Enablement to onboard partner managers and sellers on partner motions and tools.

 - Track return on partner events and programs.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL & AI-NATIVE OPS

 - Partner with Finance, Legal, Marketing, Product and Field Engineering so partner priorities are heard and consistently planned for.

 - Use AI and agentic tooling in everyday work, and help partnerships and sales teams do the same.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years in partnerships operations, strategy and operations, alliances, sales operations or consulting, including experience as a business partner to a partnerships or sales leader

 - Experience building partner pipeline reporting, attribution and forecasting, and a record of making the numbers trusted

 - Experience with co-sell, channel, alliance or marketplace motions

 - Experience running business reviews or forecast calls that produce decisions

 - Strong analytical skills, with comfort in SQL or BI tools

 - Credibility with senior leaders and the ability to influence without formal authority

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and building structure in a fast-moving startup

 - Experience building teams and processes as a business grows and scales

 - BA/BS degree in a quantitative field preferred


PREFERRED

 - Experience at an AI/ML infrastructure, developer tools, or API-first company

 - Experience with cloud marketplaces and hyperscaler co-sell programs

title: GTM Systems Lead
description:
ABOUT US

We're Team Granola 👋

Granola is an AI-powered notepad for people in back-to-back meetings. What started as a better way to take notes has become a shared workspace that helps teams capture, organize, and act on what matters.

We're building a product people genuinely love and are fortunate to work with many of the world's most ambitious companies. As we continue to grow, we're looking for a GTM Systems Lead to build the systems and data foundation that Sales, CS and leadership run on.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a GTM Systems Lead to own the technology behind Granola’s commercial team as we scale.

You’ll design, build and run the systems our Sales and CS teams rely on. Our current stack has served us well, but it needs to evolve as the team grows. You’ll take responsibility for how the tools fit together, what we build versus buy, and how information flows between them.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll set the direction of the stack and implement the technical changes that make it work. You’ll work closely with Sales, CS and Data, and report to the Head of RevOps. You won’t be limited to administering a CRM or building isolated automations: you’ll own how the whole system works.



WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and evolve the GTM stack. Decide how our Sales and CS systems should fit together, what to build versus buy, and what to prioritise as we grow.

 - Own the technical architecture of our CRM, Attio. Shape its data model, objects, workflows and integrations. You’ll be hands-on with configuration, particularly early on, but routine admin won’t be the sole focus of the role.

 - Build and maintain integrations. Make data flow reliably across Attio and our wider toolset, including Apollo, Cal.com http://Cal.com, Tally and Polytomic, and into the data systems used by the wider business.

 - Own the wider toolset. Assess new tools and vendors, improve or replace what isn’t working, and make sure the stack is useful, reliable and cost-conscious.

 - Find opportunities for automation and AI. Identify work that could be made easier for Sales and CS, and build or collaborate on solutions where they fit the priorities of the stack.

 - Keep systems dependable. Troubleshoot problems, establish sensible governance and documentation, and partner with IT on access and security.

 - Understand how teams work. Get close to Sales and CS workflows so the systems you build solve real problems, not just technical ones.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience designing, building and owning systems used by a growing commercial team. Relevant hands-on experience matters more to us than a particular number of years or experience with a specific CRM.

 - Sound judgement about system architecture, priorities and build-versus-buy decisions—and the ability to explain those decisions to non-technical colleagues.

 - Technical depth beyond administering tools: you’ve built integrations and are comfortable working with APIs, webhooks and code. Experience with SQL, Python or JavaScript would be useful.

 - An understanding of CRM data models, routing, enrichment and the operational work needed to keep data flowing reliably.

 - A willingness to get into the weeds. You’re comfortable doing the implementation yourself while also thinking about how the stack should develop over time.

 - Curiosity about AI-powered GTM workflows, with experience building them a plus rather than a prerequisite.

 - A collaborative, low-ego approach. You can work through messy requests with Sales, CS and Data, challenge assumptions constructively, and ship solutions people can use.

 - You don’t need to have used Attio or every tool in our stack. We’re more interested in what you’ve built, how you think about systems, and how you’d apply that experience here.


ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

We are living in the most exciting time for tool builders since Engelbart's demo in 1968 and we want to assemble the best crew to build this future together. Our compensation philosophy is to hire the best people in the market and pay them accordingly with salary, variable, and equity.

Lastly, we think amazing talent comes from all kinds of life journeys and experiences. If what is written above speaks to you, whether you look like a fit on paper or not, please reach out.

title: Senior Salesforce Developer
description:
Webflow is the agentic web marketing platform for modern marketing teams, helping organizations build, manage, and optimize high-performing web experiences that drive predictable growth and strengthen brand trust. Building at Webflow will need grit, because we move fast, without ever sacrificing craft or quality.

We’re looking for a Senior Salesforce Developer to help Webflow scale our go-to-market systems with quality, scalability, and strong governance. You’ll design and build the Salesforce, CPQ, and integration solutions that our Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance teams depend on every day. You’ll work closely with stakeholders and the broader Enterprise Technology team to turn business needs into clean, durable solutions.

This role combines hands-on engineering excellence with the judgment to know what to build, what to simplify, and what not to build at all. You’ll help make our platform easier to use, easier to trust, and easier to extend.

You’ll join a team of 5 architects, developers, and admins who own Webflow’s GTM systems end to end. We don’t have dedicated project managers, business analysts, or QA. Each of us runs our own projects from the first stakeholder conversation through requirements, design, build, testing, and rollout. We work as a community of practice. We share patterns, review each other’s work, and grow the craft together.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE:

 - Location: Remote-first (Canada)

 - Core working hours overlap with US Eastern / Pacific time

 - Full-time

 - Permanent

 - The cash compensation for this role is tailored to align with the cost of labor in different geographic markets. The specific base pay within the range will be determined by the candidate’s geographic location, job-related experience, knowledge, qualifications, and skills.
   
   - Canada (figures cited below are in CAD and pertain to workers in ON & BC, Canada)
     
     - $116,600-$163,300

 

This role is also eligible to participate in Webflow's company-wide bonus program. Target amounts are a percentage of base salary and vary by career level. Payouts are based on company performance against established financial and operational goals.

 

Please visit our Careers page https://webflow.com/careers#pay-zones for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

 

 - Application Information:
   
   - Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled
   
   - This posting is for an existing vacancy

 - Reporting to Anna Duncanson

 

As a Senior Salesforce Developer, you will:

 - Own the whole problem, not just the ticket. You’ll shape solutions from the first stakeholder conversation through launch, and bring your designs to a team that reviews, challenges, and builds on each other’s work.

 - Partner with RevOps, MarketingOps, LegalOps, Finance, and Pricing & Packaging leaders to turn business needs into clear designs, with options and tradeoffs that help them decide well.

 - Help own and evolve our Quote-to-Cash platform, from quoting and approvals through contracts and renewals, and help shape where Revenue Cloud Advanced fits.

 - Make the platform simpler. Reuse before you build, consolidate overlapping automation, and retire tools and packages we no longer need.

 - Design resilient integrations across the GTM tech stack, and chase data issues to their root cause even when they span several systems.

 - Build shared AI tooling that speeds up the whole team, from test generation to code review to metadata analysis.

 - Ship with care. Deploy your own changes through Gearset, build in monitoring, and fix production issues before users notice.

 - Raise the bar. Set the Apex, LWC, and security patterns others build on, give thoughtful reviews, and mentor developers and admins.

 - Help shape how we work, not just what we build. Take your turn as Scrum Master, run our ceremonies, and bring ideas that make the whole team faster and better.

 


ABOUT YOU:

Requirements:

 - BS / BA college degree or relevant experience.

 - 5+ years of hands-on Salesforce development in a complex Sales Cloud org.

 - Salesforce Platform Developer I and Platform Developer II certifications.

 - Strong Apex, SOQL, Flow, and LWC skills, and a clear sense of when to use each.

 - Deep understanding of the platform’s transaction model, including order of execution, synchronous and asynchronous processing, bulkification, and governor limits, plus experience tuning performance in large-data-volume orgs.

 - Strong grasp of Salesforce security in code, including CRUD, FLS, sharing, injection prevention, and named credentials.

 - Hands-on Salesforce CPQ experience.

 - Experience with source-driven delivery: SFDX, Git, pull request workflows, static analysis, automated testing, and rollback planning in a CI/CD tool such as Gearset or Copado.

 - Experience with event-driven patterns such as Platform Events and Change Data Capture.

 - Experience building and supporting integrations designed for failure, including retries, idempotency, error handling, and clear system-of-record boundaries.

Preferred:

 - Salesforce CPQ, Revenue Cloud, and/or Platform App Builder certifications.

 - Experience with identity provisioning or data warehouse integrations.

 - Experience in a B2B SaaS environment

 

You’ll thrive as a Senior Salesforce Developer at Webflow if you:

 - Are comfortable wearing many hats. You’re as confident running a requirements session, managing a timeline, writing test plans, and handling a production issue as you are writing code.

 - Hold a high bar for quality. You write clean, well-tested, well-documented code, and you treat production with care.

 - Design for scale. You build for where Webflow is going, not just where it is today.

 - Value strong governance. Clear standards, peer review, and documented decisions matter to you, and you help others follow them.

 - Challenge assumptions, including your own. You ask why, test ideas with data, and change course when the evidence says you should.

 - Always look for a better way. You reflect on your work and keep improving your skills, our patterns, and our processes.

 - Find the root cause. You use logs, data, and testing to prove what’s wrong before you change anything.

 - Communicate clearly. You can explain a technical tradeoff to a sales leader and to another engineer.

 - Protect focus. You redirect out-of-scope asks into intake, prioritize by value and risk, and leave room for the unplanned.

 - Help create a team where everyone feels safe to ask questions, raise concerns, and admit mistakes.

 - Stay curious and open to growth — demonstrating a proactive embrace of AI, and actively building and applying fluency in emerging technologies to elevate how we work, drive faster outcomes, and expand collective impact.




OUR CORE BEHAVIORS

 - Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first.

 - Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act.

 - Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible.

 - Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers.

 


BENEFITS

 - Ownership in what you help build. Every permanent Webflower receives equity (RSUs) in our growing, privately held company.

 - Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums.

 - Support for every stage of family life. 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions.

 - Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.

 - Wellness for the whole you. Access to mental health resources, therapy and coaching.

 - Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally.

 - Stipends to support our distributed team. Localized support for cell, Wi-Fi, and WFH expenses to help you settle into your best remote life.

Temporary employees may be eligible for paid holiday and time off, statutory leaves of absence, and company-sponsored medical benefits depending on their Fixed Term Contract and their country/state of employment.

 


BE YOU, WITH US

title: Director, EMEA Sales Operations
description:
About the Role

We're looking for a Director of EMEA Sales Operations to be the dedicated GTM Operations partner for our EMEA region. This role sits at the centre of EMEA's go-to-market motion, spanning New Logo, Growth, and Commercial/hybrid motions across a fast-growing, multi-country region.

 

You will partner directly with the VP of EMEA and the region's Account Executives, Business Development Reps, and Solutions Architects to deliver the insights, enablement, and processes that power territory design, quota allocation, pipeline and forecasting hygiene, and the region's operating cadence. Because EMEA spans many countries and time zones relative to global GTM Operations and Systems teams based in the US, this role requires someone who can operate with real autonomy, exercise judgment on what to escalate versus solve locally, and represent EMEA's specific needs (FSI and financial services-heavy Strategic accounts across UK/Ireland and DACH, multiple hybrid Commercial motions, territory splits across UK/Ireland, DACH, Nordics, and Southern Europe) back into Temporal's global GTM Operations function.

 

We're building a GTM Operations function that is AI-native from the ground up. We expect this leader to bring demonstrated experience using AI tools to accelerate analysis, surface insights, and scale operational work—not as a future aspiration, but as a core part of how they work today.

 

Responsibilities

 - Serve as the dedicated Sales Operations partner for EMEA, supporting New Logo, Growth, and Commercial/hybrid motions across the region, and knowing when to solve locally versus escalate to global GTM Operations or Systems.

 - Partner with the VP of EMEA and regional sales leadership to deliver actionable insights on net-new pipeline generation, account penetration, and territory design.

 - Own pipeline visibility and forecasting hygiene across all EMEA motions, including large complex enterprise deals, consumption workload ramps, and Commercial/self-serve pipeline.

 - Conduct white-space and TAM analysis to identify high-propensity targets across EMEA's markets, with particular attention to the region's concentration of financial services, banking, and fintech accounts.

 - Identify process gaps across the region's hunting, growth, and hybrid motions, and partner with GTM Systems to scope and implement automation—including AI-assisted workflows that reduce manual effort and increase regional coverage.

 - Analyse regional sales performance (win/loss, deal velocity, conversion, quota attainment) across segments, and translate findings into clear recommendations for the VP of EMEA and regional leaders; leverage AI tools to accelerate analysis and surface patterns at scale.

 - Build and maintain Salesforce and Omni reporting and dashboards tailored to EMEA, supporting Strategic, Growth, and Commercial views (including CQA/Tiered account, SSU, and workload metrics specific to the region).

 - Support the region's full operating cadence: forecasting calls, QBRs, pipeline reviews, and account planning sessions, often prepping leadership with regional metrics ahead of cross-timezone reviews.

 - Drive annual and in-year planning for EMEA: capacity plans, territory carving and re-carving (including account transitions as reps' territories evolve), and quota allocation across New Logo, Growth, and Commercial.

 - Evaluate new market entry and partner with regional GTM leadership on market expansion priorities, including coverage models and impacts to org design.

 
 

Qualifications

 - Experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Field Operations supporting a B2B enterprise or strategic sales organization in technology or software.

 - Proven track record supporting multiple sales motions at once: net-new logo hunting, growth/expansion within existing accounts, and self-serve or hybrid AE-assisted motions.

 - Demonstrated AI-native working style: hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Notion AI, or purpose-built GTM AI tools) to accelerate analysis, automate repeatable ops tasks, generate insights from large datasets, and improve the speed and quality of decision-making. We are not looking for theoretical familiarity—we want to see how AI is embedded in how you work today.

 - Deep experience across EMEA markets and fluency in the cultural and commercial similarities and differences across these markets.

 - Hands-on experience with building equitable territories, account scoring, quota allocation, and capacity modelling across a multi-country region.

 - Strong Salesforce expertise, including building scalable reports and dashboards across multiple sales motions and segments.

 - Highly analytical, with the ability to turn data into clear, actionable insights for regional sales leadership; comfortable pairing SQL, BI tools, and AI assistants to move faster and go deeper.

 - Strong cross-functional partner who can work effectively with regional sales and SA leadership, global GTM Operations, GTM Systems, and Marketing.

 - Comfortable presenting insights and recommendations to senior regional and global leadership.

 - Able to operate both strategically and tactically depending on business needs.

 - Bonus: experience operating in a consumption-based business, with a strong understanding of how usage impacts forecasting, pipeline, and quota planning for newly acquired and expanding accounts.

 - Bonus: experience evaluating or deploying AI-powered GTM tools (e.g., AI forecasting, account scoring, pipeline intelligence, or conversation intelligence platforms) and driving adoption across a regional sales team.

title: GTM Senior Business Systems Analyst, Marketing & Pre-Sales
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.



About the Role

Ramp is in a critical phase of growth, and marketing is one of the biggest drivers of it. We're building out our business systems team to make sure the systems behind every campaign, list, and lead can keep up. You'll work directly with Growth Marketing, Demand Generation, Lifecycle, Events, Sales Development, and Sales to own the systems that turn marketing programs into pipeline. You'll own HubSpot and how it connects to Salesforce and the rest of our GTM stack.



What You'll Do

 - Own top-of-funnel marketing systems: the roadmap, the architecture decisions inside them, and their operational health

 - Run HubSpot as a system, not just a tool: workflows, lists, forms, properties, lifecycle stages, and the permissions and naming conventions that keep it from sprawling

 - Run campaign operations end-to-end: program and campaign structure, campaign membership and status, event and webinar lead capture, and launch QA, so Marketing can ship quickly without creating data debt

 - Own workflow management in HubSpot: build, document, and audit nurture, enrollment, and suppression workflows, and retire the ones that no longer earn their place

 - Build and govern lists: ICP segmentation, inclusion and suppression logic, enrichment, and email validation between a Growth request and a send. Every list should be reproducible and explainable.

 - Own privacy and opt-out management: subscription types, consent capture, unsubscribe and opt-out handling across HubSpot, Salesforce, and sales engagement tools, and compliance with CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and CCPA in a regulated fintech environment

 - Design and maintain UTM tracking and attribution architecture: UTM taxonomy and governance, hidden-field capture on forms, lead source and original source logic, and how campaign touches flow into Salesforce, so the attribution reporting is something the business trusts

 - Build the Salesforce automation behind marketing handoffs: record-triggered flows, validation rules, fields, and permission sets

 - Use AI to automate the work where it holds up: enrichment, list QA, data quality checks, and request triage

 - Prioritize incoming requests by ROI. Decide what gets built, deferred, or declined, and show the numbers behind each call.



What You'll Need

 - 5+ years in marketing operations, business systems, or revenue operations at a fast-paced B2B company

 - Deep hands-on HubSpot experience: workflows built and debugged, and list, form, and property architecture you designed rather than inherited

 - Hands-on campaign operations experience: you've built campaign structures and owned the lists and sends behind real programs

 - A working command of email privacy and consent: subscription management, opt-out handling across systems, and the regulations behind them

 - UTM and attribution architecture you've owned in practice: taxonomy, capture, lead source logic, and the MQL-to-SQL handoff

 - Salesforce Admin experience, including flows you built and debugged when they broke (certification is a plus)

 - A habit of framing problems rather than waiting for a spec: you take on ambiguous requests, make the decisions, and ship

 - You dissect a problem, drive it to completion with little supervision, and can explain the tradeoffs to any audience



Nice to Have

 - Enrichment and routing tools such as Clay, ZoomInfo, LeanData and Chili Piper

 - Sales engagement and automation platforms such as Outreach and Workato

 - Deliverability and list hygiene at high sending volume

 - Paid media and ad platform integrations, including conversion tracking

 - Lead scoring and MQL model design

 - Snowflake, Looker, or similar BI and warehouse tools

 - Linear or similar project management software




BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend




UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
   
   


CANADA

 - Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life

 - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

 - Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime)

 - Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay

 - Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health




UNITED KINGDOM

 - Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite

 - Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi

 - Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay




REFERRAL INSTRUCTIONS

If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf.

 


OTHER NOTICES

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

 

Beware of recruiting scams: Ramp will only contact you through official @Ramp.com http://Ramp.com email addresses and will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information during the hiring process.

title: Revenue Operations Lead
description:
ABOUT POSH

We are all social creatures, but the dominant “social” companies today have evolved into digital loneliness machines, driving isolation, anxiety, and mental health challenges around the world.

Human connection is lost. Posh is a beacon guiding us back.

Posh enables anyone to build an IRL community based on shared interests, while connecting consumers with the communities of people just like them. Founded by event organizers who were frustrated with the growing loneliness epidemic and the tools available to build their own event brand, we’ve built the ultimate platform for launching, monetizing, and finding IRL communities of people just like you. In just 6 years, Posh has grown to a team of 70, expanded to 10M+ users, secured $70m in venture funding, and facilitated over $400M in transactions.





ABOUT THE ROLE

As Revenue Operations Lead, you’ll own the systems, tooling, and enablement that Posh’s GTM teams run on every day. You’ll be the person who knows how the CRM is wired, why a lead routed where it did, which dashboards leadership trusts, and what a new rep needs in their first 30 days to ramp.

Your primary mandate is the GTM tech stack and the data in it: architecture, automation, integrations, reporting, hygiene, and the enablement that gets teams actually using it. Alongside that, you’ll own the operational side of compensation and planning: administering commissions and quotas, building quota and capacity models, and supporting annual and quarterly planning with clean numbers and working tooling.

You’ll report to the Head of Finance, partner closely with GTM leadership, and be the day-to-day point person for Sales, Customer Success, Account Management, Marketing, and Support.

This is an in-person position (5 days a week) at our SoHo, NYC office.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN & ACHIEVE

 - Own the GTM systems stack: Administer and architect the CRM and surrounding tools (prospecting, enrichment, routing, sequencing, CS platform, forecasting, reporting, AI tooling) while auditing to ensure data accuracy. Own integrations, automation, permissions, field design, and the roadmap for what we buy, build, or retire.

 - Keep the data decision-ready: Define object models, lifecycle stages, and data standards across the funnel. Run CRM hygiene, dedupe, and data quality monitoring so pipeline, forecast, and account data can be trusted without manual cleanup.

 - Run enablement: Own onboarding and ramp for new GTM hires, ongoing training on process and tooling, playbook and collateral management, and adoption tracking. Make sure every process you ship is one the team actually uses.

 - Build reporting and dashboards: Deliver the standard set of pipeline, funnel, forecast, activity, and post-sale (NRR, churn, renewals, adoption) reporting that leadership runs on, and make it self-serve where possible.

 - Administer compensation and commissions: Own monthly and quarterly commission calculations, comp plan documentation, rep disputes and exceptions, and SPIF tracking. Partner with Finance on accuracy, accruals, and payout timing, and on plan design changes.

 - Own quota and capacity models: Build and maintain quota allocation, territory and book-of-business assignments, ramp assumptions, and capacity models. Keep them current as headcount, segments, and targets change.

 - Support planning cycles: Provide the data, models, and tooling behind annual and quarterly GTM planning (headcount, quotas, coverage, pipeline targets), and translate approved plans into CRM configuration, quotas, and reporting.

 - Own channel attribution and conversion: Know every path an organizer takes to Posh (outbound, inbound, paid, affiliates, Campus, events, renewals). Make sure every lead and deal is tagged to the right source and owner. Maintain one GMV attribution model for all teams, and track conversion by channel from first touch to first event live.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4–7 years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM Systems, including at least 2 years as the primary admin or architect of a CRM in a high-growth environment

 - Deep hands-on expertise in HubSpot (objects, workflows, automation, integrations, permissions, reporting), plus familiarity with the surrounding stack (enrichment, sequencing, routing, CS, and forecasting tools)

 - Experience building and running GTM enablement: onboarding, ramp programs, process training, and driving tool adoption

 - Experience administering commissions and quotas, with a working understanding of comp plan mechanics, accelerators, clawbacks, and SPIFs

 - Comfort building quota, capacity, and territory models in spreadsheets and supporting planning cycles with clean, defensible numbers

 - Strong data and reporting skills: SQL or equivalent, dashboard building, and the ability to turn messy CRM data into clear operating decisions

 - A builder mentality with a bias toward shipping, documenting, and iterating; comfortable managing a small team and working cross-functionally with Finance, Product, Data, and GTM leadership


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a high-growth marketplace, fintech, or consumer technology company

 - Experience implementing or migrating a CRM, Customer Success, or commissions platform

 - Experience with lightweight GTM engineering: scripting, APIs, Zapier/Clay-style automation, or AI-assisted workflows

 - Experience scaling GTM operations through Series B to Series D

 - Experience building RevOps processes from an earlier stage of maturity
