title: GTM Operations & Agentic Workflows
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

The GTM Agentic Workflows team is building OpenAI’s agentic go-to-market operating system. We work with sellers, GTM leaders, and partners in GTM Systems, Data Science, and Product to connect customer intelligence to account strategy, helping teams prioritize opportunities, grow adoption across accounts, and spend time where it matters most.

About the Role

As an individual contributor on the GTM Agentic Workflows team, you’ll own the design, rollout, and performance of processes and workflows across the customer lifecycle, from lead routing through deal execution, delivery, and consumption. Orchestration is central to this role. You’ll bring sellers, GTM leaders, and cross-functional partners together around a shared outcome, then connect the work of people, systems, and agentic workflows to deliver it.

In this role, you will:

 - Prioritize problems with GTM leaders and the field. Look at where sellers repeat work, where deals stall, and which handoffs break down. Use the frequency and impact of those problems to decide what to tackle first.

 - Strengthen the foundations of GTM workflows. Set the strategy for enriching person and company data, and partner with GTM Systems on lead routing and how sellers manage accounts and opportunities in Salesforce.

 - Orchestrate delivery across teams. Align owners on the outcome, sequence work across functions, and resolve competing priorities. Make clear who decides, what information carries forward, and when the next team can act.

 - Design and launch workflows with Product and Enterprise Systems. Define what triggers the workflow, what information an agent needs, and when a person should review or approve an action. Pilot with field teams and partner with Enablement on rollout.

 - Own performance after launch. Measure adoption alongside outcomes such as lead response time, accuracy of proposed updates, and time to complete a handoff. Use those results and field feedback to decide what to improve next.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 8+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or related roles at a high-growth technology company

 - Strong systems thinking with deep experience designing and scaling sales systems, processes, and workflows across the full sales lifecycle

 - Experience taking a multi-step GTM workflow from a field problem through rollout. You can explain what you automated, where people retained judgment, and how you measured whether it worked.

 - Strong proficiency in Salesforce and data tools (e.g., SQL, Excel). Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail

 - Experience with territory design, account structures, and pipeline management

title: Go to Market Systems Admin (HubSpot)
description:
Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you


TO BE A TEYAN

We are not just a fintech company. We develop people by giving them the autonomy and the responsibility to challenge the status quo, so they can be the main actors of the change we want to bring to the market.

We are always looking for people better than us to join the team, disrupt payments, and revolutionise commerce in Europe. The goal we share, the mission is one, and at the end of the day we are just people trying to help other people.




WHAT IS YOUR MISSION?

Our sales agents are on the front lines, talking to merchants every day. Across the go to market systems they use to manage their sales, HubSpot CRM is where their deals, activities, conversations, reporting, automations and portfolio lives. When HubSpot works, our salespeople sell. When it breaks quietly in the background, deals stall, data drifts, and the people who trust the numbers stop trusting the tool.

Your mission is to be the guardian of that system. You are the person who keeps HubSpot healthy, honest, and trustworthy, so that every seller and every leader can rely on it without ever thinking about it.

This is not a caretaking job where you wait for tickets and tick them off. You are a detective and a builder. You go looking for what is wrong before anyone reports it, you find the real reason something failed instead of patching the symptom, and you make sure the same failure never happens twice. You turn a messy, growing CRM into a system people can trust, and you can prove it with data.




AS THE GUARDIAN OF OUR CRM YOU WILL

Investigate root causes, not symptoms. When something in HubSpot fails, you own it. You dig into what actually went wrong, validate the real root cause, and drive it to a fix. You are the single point of contact when the CRM misbehaves, and nothing gets dropped on your watch.

Prevent the next bug before it happens. You do not just close errors, you learn from them. You spot the patterns, harden the implementations that keep breaking, and put guardrails in place so a whole class of problems disappears. Every automation and implementation, local or global, follows our guidelines because you make sure it does, before and after it goes live.

Measure the health of the CRM. You build the dashboards that show, at a glance, whether what we ship actually works and keeps working. You track error rates, adoption, and data quality over time, so CRM health stops being a feeling and becomes a number we can watch and improve.

Turn data into action. You are as comfortable reading the numbers as fixing the system. You globalise and clean up our reporting once the requirements from Commercial Excellence are aligned, retire the dashboards no one needs, and use data to find the problems no one has noticed yet.

Build and improve, hands on. You create new automations and refine the ones we have, you read the logic of a workflow well enough to debug it, and you keep the instance clean, governed, and scalable across every market in Europe.

Your goal is to maximise the value and the trust in the CRM our salespeople rely on. Your success is measured in the health of the platform: fewer recurring failures, faster time to a real fix, cleaner data, and leaders who believe the numbers again because someone is watching them every day.




WHAT IS YOUR STORY?

You need to be eager to learn and improve every day. Some qualities you must have:

 - A detective's instinct: you are not satisfied with a symptom, you want the root cause, and you enjoy the hunt

 - An owner's mindset: you do not wait to be told, you know the instance and you act on it

 - Reactive when it counts and proactive by default: when something breaks you are on it and you meet the SLA, and when you see a risk you raise it before it spreads

 - Data-driven and analytical: you read data, understand the problem, and propose the fix

 - The confidence to challenge a request rather than just take it, because requests will not only come from us, and the right thing to build is your job to protect

 - Experience with a CRM (HubSpot ideal, Salesforce or similar is welcome), with ticketing and SLAs, and comfort building automations and reading the logic behind them

This is not a deep-specialist or heavy-code role. Understanding custom code is a plus, but the heart of the job is investigation, prevention, reporting, and governance. If you get satisfaction from taking something messy and making it trustworthy, this is your role.

Teya is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or background can thrive and do their best work. We believe that a diverse team leads to better ideas, stronger outcomes, and a more supportive workplace for all.

If you require any reasonable adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process whether for interviews, assessments, or other parts of the application—we encourage you to let us know. We are committed to ensuring that every candidate has a fair and accessible experience with us.

description:

To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is seeking a Senior Marketing Operations Specialist to rethink how campaigns get done. You already understand how campaign operations work: intake, program build, QA, launch and reporting. You will build much of it yourself and partner with Marketing Technology, Marketing Intelligence and regional teams to scale it.

The ideal candidate is a strong Marketo practitioner who thinks in systems, asks why a process exists before changing it, and is comfortable replacing manual steps with tools that work reliably at scale.

YOU'RE A GREAT FIT IF YOU:
3+ years in marketing operations, campaign operations or marketing automation, with deep experience running campaign programs end to end.

Working knowledge of how campaign operations work across intake, planning, build, QA, launch and reporting, and an understanding of where these processes typically slow down.

Experience using AI tools or agents to automate or accelerate operational work, with results you can describe.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:
Map current operations and stakeholder needs: Review how Snowflake plans, builds, launches and reports on campaigns today, including Marketo programs, templates, intake, Wrike workflows and dashboards. Interview campaign managers, regional and field marketing, sales operations and marketing intelligence to find friction, workarounds and priorities.

Reimagine the workflow: Design a future-state campaign operating model that uses agents, dashboards, automation and apps to replace manual steps. Build and deliver: Build workflows and automations in Marketo, Salesforce and the broader martech stack, and pilot them with a small group of users before scaling. Partner with Marketing Intelligence, Sales Operations, Marketing Technology and IT to align the design with enterprise data and systems. Own the documentation, controls and training needed for adoption.

Fluency in funnel reporting, lead routing and lead scoring, including how lifecycle stages, routing rules and scores affect campaign follow-up.
Fluency in Salesforce campaigns, including campaign hierarchy, member statuses, and how campaign membership relates to Marketo program membership and lead or contact records.
Working knowledge of SQL for exploring marketing data.
Experience with Workato, Zapier, Tray.io http://Tray.io or another workflow platform.
Experience building or piloting AI agents or LLM-based workflows with a measured outcome.
Experience building dashboards or lightweight internal apps that operations teams use.
Familiarity with attribution, ABM or intent data.
Experience with Wrike, Asana or another work-management platform.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:
First 30 days: Map current campaign operations, complete the first round of stakeholder interviews, and identify the highest-friction handoffs.
First 60 days: Publish a future-state workflow design with requirements, priorities and success metrics, and secure stakeholder alignment on the first two or three changes.

pay: CA$305K – CA$365K • Offers Equity • Multiple Ranges
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


THE ROLE

You'll lead marketing operations and analytics at Cohere. That covers the team, the martech stack, how we measure marketing's contribution to pipeline, and the budget and pipeline numbers marketing plans against. When leadership asks what marketing produced last quarter and what to fund next, the answer starts with your numbers.

The role reports to the VP of Brand. You'll work most closely with the Marketing Chief of Staff and the heads of Growth and Demand and Product Marketing, and every week with Revenue Operations, Sales Operations & Finance. Web operations is part of marketing but doesn't report to this role.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN



THE TEAM

You'll manage the marketing operations, automation, and analytics and data operations staff, and hire where you find gaps. Marketing is growing rapidly, so you'll also bring acquired companies' systems and data into our stack.



MEASUREMENT

The attribution methodology is yours, documented and signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. Each quarter you'll present marketing's pipeline contribution to the executive team and say what you'd change. Your analysts do the same for the program teams in Growth and Demand, Events and Product Marketing, showing which campaigns and channels are paying back their spend.



SYSTEMS AND DATA

Marketo, Looker, GA4 and 6sense are yours end to end, along with the campaign and lead side of Salesforce. That includes forms, nurture, lead lifecycle, scoring and routing. Campaign data needs to be structured well enough that analysts don't need workarounds, and target-account data has to reconcile to the governed account list. With Revenue Operations, you'll make sure the data behind marketing's pipeline numbers can't change without a record, so a bulk edit can't quietly rewrite marketing's results. A/B testing on nurture and forms sits with you too, sized so the results can be read.

Over time we want fewer tools and fewer dashboards, with one governed source for each metric.



BUDGET AND PLANNING NUMBERS

You'll own the martech and operations budget and track budget and headcount across marketing. You'll also build the pipeline and capacity models marketing plans against. The Marketing Chief of Staff runs planning and the business reviews and leads the trade-off conversations with your numbers in hand. Marketing and Sales need to count pipeline the same way, every time.



YOUR FIRST YEAR


In the first 90 days, you'll document the attribution methodology and get it signed off by Marketing, Revenue Operations and Finance. By then we should also have an inventory of every reporting surface, each with a named owner, and your order for fixing the data problems you inherit.

By three months, one governed executive dashboard has replaced the competing decks in business reviews, and rebuilt lead routing is in production.

By six months, target-account reporting reconciles to the governed list, and anyone on the team can reproduce quarterly attribution from the documented method, with change control on the data underneath it. The stack is smaller than when you arrived, and some marketing workflows run on agents in production. Annual planning runs on your budget, headcount and pipeline models.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



MUST HAVE

 - 10+ years in marketing operations or marketing analytics in B2B or enterprise software, including at least one high-growth company.

 - You've managed a marketing operations and analytics team and its martech budget, setting priorities across ops, automation and analytics specialists and hiring to fill gaps.

 - Hands-on Marketo and Salesforce experience with lead lifecycle, campaign structure, routing and the sync between the two. You've configured these systems yourself.

 - You've owned a multi-touch attribution model end to end and defended its definitions to a CFO or executive team.

 - SQL, and enough comfort in a governed BI layer like Looker to check a number yourself before you present it.

 - You've run the data side of an account-based motion, including the hygiene that makes a target account list reportable.

 - You've worked closely with Revenue Operations and Sales Operations without duplicating their work.

 - Experience in enterprise, regulated or public-sector buying environments, including GDPR and CASL as they apply to lead handling.

 - You already use AI and automation in your own team's work.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Enterprise AI, infrastructure or developer-platform marketing.

 - You've built agentic or LLM-based workflows in GTM operations and measured what they saved.

 - Product-led funnel instrumentation running alongside a sales-led pipeline.

 - You've consolidated an inherited martech stack, or merged systems after an acquisition.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. title: Member of Technical Staff (GTM Engineer, Growth)
description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and the Growth team owns the loops that turn that adoption into lasting usage and revenue.

We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer to build the systems that turn product usage into revenue and turn self-serve usage into enterprise pipeline. You'll turn first-party Computer and Enterprise usage into account-level signals. You'll ship the in-product paths that capture sales intent, and build and validate those signals with data science. Alongside product engineers, you ship production code, instrument the product and run experiments. You'll partner closely with Revenue Operations, who own Salesforce, CPQ, routing and sales reporting.

Tech Stack: TypeScript | Next.js | React | Python | PostgreSQL | Snowflake | Eppo | AWS




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build account-level PLG signals: map users and workspaces to accounts, and define the activation, expansion and intent signals that predict an enterprise deal. Publish them as trusted models that sales use for scoring and routing.

 - Own the in-product paths from self-serve to sales, like contact-sales entry points, high-intent upsells and meeting booking, across web and app. Decide who sees them, when and with what context, and measure them end to end, from surface to booked meeting to pipeline.

 - Lead experiments end to end on sales-assist surfaces and targeting, from hypothesis and instrumentation through analysis and rollout. Partner with Data Science to measure meetings and qualified opportunities, not just clicks.

 - Build the internal tools and automation Growth and GTM teams run on

 - Partner closely with Sales, Sales Systems, Data Science, Marketing and Product to turn product signals into pipeline. Be upstream partner to sales systems that own Salesforce, CPQ and routing


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 2+ years as a growth, GTM, data or full-stack engineer, shipping production code (TypeScript/React, Python).

 - Strong SQL and comfort building data models in a warehouse (Snowflake, dbt-style).

 - Experience instrumenting product events and running A/B experiments end to end.

 - Commercial instinct: you start from a revenue problem ("trial-to-enterprise conversion won't move") and work back to the signal or surface that fixes it.

 - Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks and integrating third-party GTM tools.

 - Operator mindset: you talk to customers directly, ship fixes, and don't need a PM to translate requests.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in a PLG-to-enterprise motion: product-qualified leads, scoring users into accounts, sales-assist flows.

 - Experience as a GTM or growth engineer at a B2B SaaS or GTM-tooling company.

 - Entity resolution, dedup or domain enrichment.

title: Growth GTM Engineer, Revenue Operations
description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. To turn that demand into pipeline, every lead has to be enriched, scored, and routed to the right next step within minutes.

We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer on the Revenue Operations team to own the lead-to-engagement engine: the enrichment platform that completes every marketing and product lead, the routing that sends each lead to nurture or to BDRs and Sales, and the syncs that move data from our warehouse into Salesforce and our GTM tools. You'll also put lead and account scores to work with Data Science, who own the scoring models, and help deliver our BDRs' prospecting tools.

You'll report to the Head of Pipeline Operations, who sets the priorities for this work and owns our marketing automation platform, campaign operations and attribution.

You'll build mostly with AI, so we care more about your instinct for go-to-market systems than your depth in any one programming language. You'll measure everything you build against meetings, pipeline and revenue.

Tech stack: Salesforce | Clay | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Snowflake | SQL | Python | Computer | LLM APIs




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the enrichment platform. Design and run waterfall enrichment across third-party providers, AI research agents and first-party data for every marketing and product lead. Handle lead-to-account matching, deduplication, field governance, data freshness and provider cost. Publish enriched data to the warehouse for Data Science and other teams to use.

 - Own lead routing. Design the decision logic that sends each lead, from marketing programs or product usage, to Marketing for nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager for engagement, based on score, segment, territory, account ownership, capacity and existing opportunities. Co-define lifecycle stages, handoff SLAs, recycle rules and speed-to-lead triggers with the Head of Pipeline Operations, and enforce them in Salesforce and our routing tools, with MQLs and PQLs on the same lifecycle and SLAs. Deliver the enrichment, signals, routing and alerts behind our account-based plays.

 - Own the syncs between our warehouse and our GTM tools. Build and maintain the reverse ETL syncs, APIs and webhooks that move data from Snowflake into Salesforce, marketing automation, routing and engagement tools. Build on the models the Data team publishes, and make sure every synced field has one owner and every sync is monitored. Support the rollout of our first marketing automation platform by building its Salesforce sync and warehouse feeds, along with the nurture enrollment rules and campaign tracking the Head of Pipeline Operations designs.

 - Put lead and account scores to work. Data Science owns our scoring models, including product-qualified lead scoring. Partner with them on marketing-qualified lead scoring by bringing in enrichment data, marketing engagement and Sales feedback, and help set the thresholds that trigger action. Make sure scores and their reasons reach Salesforce on time and that Sales understands them.

 - Close the feedback loop. Track the funnel from lead creation to closed-won. Find where leads stall, which sources and signals predict pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold, then feed that back into routing, Marketing programs and Data Science's scoring work. Capture the campaign and touchpoint data behind attribution, which the Head of Pipeline Operations owns.

 - Help deliver the BDR prospecting toolset. It combines vendor solutions and internal applications. The Head of Pipeline Operations owns these systems, and BDR leadership decides the sequences and plays that run on them. Implement the vendor tools and integrate them with Salesforce and our data. Build the workflows and agents around them, such as signal-triggered alerts, prioritized outreach queues and pre-call research briefs. Resolve the system and data issues that slow reps down. Supply our GTM Platform team, which builds our rep-facing applications, with the data, signals and requirements they need. Talk to users, track adoption and retire what doesn't get used.

 - Partner across the business. Work with Marketing, Growth, BDR and Sales leadership, Data Science, Data Engineering, GTM Platform and Sales Systems to turn messy processes into durable systems, and use the scores and product usage signals Data Science and Growth publish to drive routing.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first 30 days:

 - Audit enrichment coverage, routing rules, warehouse-to-Salesforce syncs and lead SLAs, and document the gaps that cost us pipeline.

In your first 60 days:

 - Ship an enrichment waterfall with measurable gains in fill rate and accuracy.

 - Ship routing that sends every marketing and product lead to nurture or sales within an agreed SLA, with dashboards for speed to lead and conversion by route.

 - Take ownership of the syncs that write scores and lead fields to Salesforce, with monitoring and one owner per field.

 - Work with Data Science to bring enrichment and marketing engagement data into MQL scoring.

In your first 90 days:

 - Ship at least one prospecting workflow or agent with sustained weekly use by BDRs and AEs.

 - Show a measurable lift in lead-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion for both MQLs and PQLs.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years in GTM engineering, RevOps or Marketing Ops engineering, growth engineering, or data engineering in B2B SaaS, including 2+ years building enrichment, routing or integration systems.

 - Commercial instinct. You start from a revenue problem and work back to the data, logic or tool that fixes it.

 - Working SQL. You pull your own data from a warehouse (Snowflake or similar) and build on the models other teams publish.

 - AI-first builder. You've shipped integrations, automations or agents that real users depend on, using AI coding tools, and you can read, review and debug what you ship. Language depth matters less than GTM judgment.

 - Deep working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns, ownership), and experience automating and integrating with it.

 - Hands-on experience with enrichment and intent tools (Clay, ZoomInfo, Apollo, 6sense, Common Room or similar), routing and scheduling tools (Default, Chili Piper, LeanData) and reverse ETL (Hightouch, Census).

 - Fluency with funnel mechanics: lifecycle design, routing logic, score thresholds, SLAs, attribution data and conversion metrics.

 - Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, rate limits and error handling.

 - Operator mindset. You work directly with reps and marketers, ship fixes quickly, and don't need a PM to translate requests.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Hybrid PLG and sales-led motions: product-qualified leads, user-to-account mapping and sales-assist routing.

 - LLM-powered research, personalization or qualification agents, including evaluation and monitoring.

 - Working alongside a data science team on lead or account scoring.

 - dbt, or production work in Python or TypeScript.

 - Entity resolution and domain matching at scale.

 - A prior GTM Engineer role at a GTM-tooling or AI-native company.

title: GTM Engineer
description:

Our global community is comprised of over 6,500 companies accessing our technology in over 140+ countries & territories. PartsBase offers a FULLY remote environment where one can work at the forefront of where the aviation business meets technology. Imagine getting to work with peers worldwide, implementing business technology projects that challenge the boundaries.

One of the top benefits of working at PartsBase is the culture. We are a TEAM-focused organization, and everyone celebrates each other's successes. Our inclusive culture welcomes all employees and values their unique contributions to our success. Our clients tell us time and time again that our people set us apart from the competition. We naturally strive to hire the very best talent.
